**The ninth-pome power lock** (PT-72, ruled 2026-11-13: kept as built and documented). `HarbingerPathPermissions.isChoiceUnresolved` reads the total of counted pomes over every Bloom (`getTotalPomesConsumed`), not the per-Bloom Communion count. From the ninth until the path is `APOTHEOS` or `SILENTIUM` (Degree 8), no manipulation answers except `conjure_staff` (`BloodManipulation.passBodyGates`), and no rite starts except the Rite of Apotheos (`CardinalRiteActivation`, `CardinalRiteCompletionEffects`, `PuppeteerTrialRiteController`). It holds a Silence through both Vesper phases and a player who split nine pomes over two Blooms without Communion. Living Staff weapon forms still change by selecting them on the wheel (`ChangeSelectedManipPacket` calls `LivingStaffWeaponFormHelper.applySelection` and does not pass the lock), so a Silence fights Vesper with the Living Arsenal and no manipulations. The warning reads the same total (`HarbingerPathPermissions.nextPomeLocks`): eating the eighth counted pome says `message.hemomancy.qliphoth_pome_item.the_ninth_husk_will_lock` in chat, and the owner's pomes show the same line in their tooltip until the ninth.

Creative-spawned / untagged pomes do not have a real bloom origin, so they use a synthetic test origin and still advance the same capability path. Their husk message is inferred from the player's current total pome count before consumption, so creative testing still displays the correct `[huskname]` message for the next pome in order.

**Stage 5 — Rite of Apotheos Unlocked**
`CardinalRiteActivation.tryStart` (server-side rite activation) checks `IInitiatoryDegree#isQliphothCommunionDone()` before allowing the `apotheos_rite` to begin. `CardinalRiteCompletionEffects.commonRefusal` repeats the same check before granting Degree 8, so old active rites or alternate completion paths cannot bypass the gate. If absent, the player receives: *"The Eighth Degree remains sealed. Consume all nine Qliphoth husks from a single bloom."* If present (and degree ≥ 7), the rite proceeds normally. Choosing the Eighth Degree from the core-witness whisper (`archon_choice_eighth_degree`) also opens the Liber's Truth entry (`LiberEntryDefinitions.TRUTH`, source `DIALOGUE`; PT-82, ruled 2026-11-13), so the Rite of Apotheos is discovered and a blank Mnemonic Blueprint takes it at `APOTHEOS_PENDING`. The D6 Rite of the Eternal Covenant shares that gate (`RiteDiscoveryRules`) and is discovered at the same moment.

Degree rites at Degrees 5 and 6 may foreshadow the growth, but Degree 7 does not drop a Spine. Consuming the ninth pome from one bloom completes Qliphoth Communion and grants the Fungal Spine once; this happens before either endgame rite.

If the initial grant cannot fit, it remains pending until inventory space opens; it is not dropped into the world. Retry ticks require a living player and an actual carried Spine before marking delivery. Creative full-inventory discard and dead-player ticks retain the pending first claim through saved degree data and death cloning. An already-carried legacy Spine fulfills the claim without adding another. An owner who loses an already granted Spine can sneak-use the original living Bloom empty-handed after consuming its nine husks. Recovery requires that Bloom's lifecycle, completed Communion and inventory space, and refuses another claim while a Spine is carried. A replacement Bloom at the same coordinates does not inherit the claim. The undecided spent-Bloom hint names Gardens travel and empty-handed sneak-use in a short action-bar line.

**Stage 6 - Silent Refusal (Pruning, Vesper, then Degree-8 Silentium)**
After the first projection, choosing Silence records `SILENT_PENDING`. Striking the owned living Bloom with any of the seven base Living Weapon forms temporarily reshapes that weapon into the Living Sickle; a second deliberate cut on the same bound Bloom changes it to severed/portal-open. Only its owner can enter the separate 50x50 barrier-floor arena in the Chamber dimension. The fight spawns one owned Crowned Refusal, transfers the ordeal identity into the Evening Star phase, and prevents duplicate Vespers on retry. Death, logout, manual exit, or restart clears the active encounter but leaves the portal open. Verified phase-two victory grants Memory of Vesper exactly once and seals the severed Bloom as an inert trophy; the path stays `SILENT_PENDING`. Absorbing that memory through the Iron Brazier permanently grants `conjure_sickle` in the fixed interior radial ring and advances the player to Degree 8 with `SILENTIUM`, which changes the Chamber to the Silent theme and grants `degree_8_silentium`. Creative players may remove the trophy for administration.

The one-time Memory of Vesper waits for inventory space as an earned `PlayerPersisted` claim. Login and one-second server retries deliver only to a living player and clear only after an actual inventory count increase. Explicit pending claims from the older root-level flag migrate on login, retry or death before cloning; Creative discard and dead-player ticks cannot consume them. Victory/ending state alone does not infer a replacement claim. Memories already lost under the old behavior cannot be reconstructed safely.

The returned revelation warns before selection that neither answer completes its path: refusal requires the owned Bloom and both Vesper phases, while the eighth Degree requires the Rite of Apotheos. The Silence confirmation teaches the base-weapon/temporary-Sickle second cut and wound entry, and states that the Silence finishes only when Vesper's memory is drawn in. Existing pending whispers use the same translated line keys, so this clarification also appears in previously saved decisions.

Pruning handles only a living Bloom. Once the second cut opens the wound, ordinary use reaches the existing owner/path-checked portal even with the restored Living Weapon still held. Logout before that second cut restores the temporary form to its original Staff; reshape it and repeat the first cut to resume. The native held-weapon entry was verified, but that test player subsequently died: saved pending refusal and the open wound persisted, while recovery of the dropped inventory remains unverified.

**Key fields serialized inside the player's `IInitiatoryDegree` capability:**

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|-----|------|---------|
| `pome_communion_done` | Boolean | Communion completed; Apotheos rite now accessible |
| `pome_communion_progress` | CompoundTag | Per-bloom pome consumption counters (keys = bloom origin Long as String) |
| `pome_communion_progress_by_bloom` | CompoundTag | The same counters keyed by bloom id (as String) |
| `pome_empowerment_expiry` | Long | Game-time tick when pome manipulation discount expires (0 = none) |
| `pome_total_consumed` | Int | Total pome counter for HUD display, capped at 9 |
| `archon_path` | Enum | `NONE`, `SILENT_PENDING`, `SILENTIUM`, `APOTHEOS_PENDING`, or `APOTHEOS`; canonical persisted route state. A Harbinger reset clears it with the Spine, the revelation and the Mycophant hunt (`resetEndgameState`) |
| `fungal_spine_granted` | Boolean | Ninth-pome Spine grant has occurred |
| `fungal_revelation_witnessed` | Boolean | First projection completed and the post-return choice was presented |

### 5.10 Endgame Bosses: Vesper and The Mycophant

The two new endgame bosses represent the fork after Archon revelation:

| Route | Boss | Entity IDs | Current status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Silent refusal (ends in Degree-8 Silentium) | **Vesper** | `hemomancy:vesper_crowned_refusal` -> `hemomancy:vesper_evening_star` | `Implemented`: entered through the Living Sickle cut and owner-bound Severed Qliphoth; retry, victory, reward, seal, and the Silentium ascension by memory absorption are wired. |
| Apotheos / fungal ascension | **The Mycophant** | `hemomancy:mycophant` | `Implemented`: entered by the fifteen-minute Gardens hunt (or a Fruiting Lure); the waking, two-phase claim/joining fight, split, yielding, succession and rewards are wired. |

**Vesper, The Crowned Refusal -> Vesper, The Evening Star**
- Represents the Archon who reaches the threshold and refuses to dissolve into the fungal reproductive cycle.
- Phase 1 (`VesperTheCrownedRefusalEntity`) is mapped from the old `XanthousKing` reference. It has no final loot and is never brought to 0 health: its health stops at a floor under each wound, and when the third wound breaks it turns invulnerable and cocoons into phase 2.
- Phase 2 (`VesperTheEveningStarEntity`) is mapped from the old `TrueXanthousKing` reference. He is not killed: a lethal blow leaves him at 1 health, downed and waiting, and the player ends the ordeal by drawing him out with Blood Absorption (`VesperCombatRules.DEFEAT_ABSORPTION_REQUIRED`); the entity is then removed without dying. On that victory the ordeal manager grants Memory of Vesper once, gives 180 experience points on every completed ordeal (`VesperOrdealManager.VICTORY_XP`; the Evening Star's own death experience is 0 and it has no loot table, ruled 2026-11-13, CR-22) and seals the source Bloom only after verifying the owner and open portal.
- **Phase 1, the Crowned Refusal (Vesper riding his mount).** One controller (`VesperMountController`) owns the mount's movement, facing and move timeline; no vanilla goals compete for the body and the AI is never switched off. Every ground move is a `BossMoveTimeline` (wind-up, active, recovery) from `VesperMountControllerRules`: the aim tracks the target at a capped turn rate during the wind-up and locks at the commit tick, so committed lunges can be sidestepped. Higher-priority beats (a wound opening, wing growth) never cut an active swing: they queue, stagger a wind-up, or take over at recovery. A lost target lets a committed move play out, then the mount patrols the arena. Old saves that persisted `NoAI` load with it cleared.
- **Telegraphs.** Every ground move shows its wind-up in the authored suite (`VesperVisualEffects`): lanes for Royal Scuttle and the grab, a cone for Pincer Vice, rings for Brood Trample and the Carapace Aneurysm, a glowing marker on every Stinger Script spike point a full volley before it erupts, and strings lowering onto each puppet landing point before a muster. Each move also sounds at its first tick.
- **Flight (from 50% health).** Wing growth flares two pairs of veined wings. Sorties use velocity steering (`VesperFlightSteeringRules`): a capped turn rate, eased acceleration and arrival, and synced bank and pitch the mount and rider lean into. Circling follows banked arcs, the Tail Fusillade is a strafing run across the mark, the Diving Rend brakes with cupped wings and then commits to a straight, unsteered dive, and landings flare into a short skid.
- **Burrow.** Vesper tucks low and grips the mount's nape (his Crossbar hand lets go) and the mount plunges into the floor. A fissure trail (`VesperBurrowRules`, `VesperBurrow`) hunts the target for 10-15 seconds, surfacing in alternating strikes, each with its own stall-and-swell tell: **claw rakes** (armour-ignoring `hemomancy:vesper_rend`, 9) and **tail stings** (6, poison and blood loss). Then the trail falls silent, the ground rumbles (a rising camera shake for players standing over the arena) and the eruption point locks partway through the rumble. The mount bursts up beneath it for 22 damage and a hard launch, then needs about 3.5 seconds to gather itself. Every second Diving Rend drives on into the floor as a 5-7 second burrow. Underground the mount is invisible, unhittable and non-colliding; a reload mid-burrow surfaces it into recovery. On the ordeal floor the trail also tears a glowing crack (`VesperBurrowFissureRenderer`); elsewhere only the chip particles (blackstone-toned flakes and grit from the authored suite) carry it. A summoned Vesper outside the ordeal surfaces on the actual ground under the trail rather than at his spawn height.
- **Wounds (70%, 40%, 10% health; ruled 2026-11-13, CR-19).** On 520 health the bands are 156 / 156 / 156, and the last 52 HP sit under the third wound. `VesperCombatRules.anchorThresholds` is read by the bar's notches too; the grounded burrow opens at 68%, 2% under the first wound, and the shorter idle starts at the second. Each threshold splits a wound open at its own place on the mount (`VesperWoundRules`): the carapace behind the throne, the throat seam, and under the tail base. The mount staggers and shrieks; scute plates hinge back from a pulsing blood core (`VesperWoundLayer`). Ordinary blows cannot hurt him while a wound is open, so the whole body says so: mount and rider wear an additive blood skin (`VesperWoundDrawLayer`, shader `entity/vesper_wound_draw`) whose vessels beat toward the wound and quicken as it drains, and nearby players get an action-bar hint to hold Blood Absorption on it. The player drains the wound by holding **Blood Absorption** on it (`VesperBloodAbsorptionInteractions`, owner-only in the ordeal): a visible blood stream runs to their hand or staff and feeds them a little blood. Hits on the wound keep it from scabbing and drain it only at a 10% fallback rate, so no build soft-locks; killing one of his puppets tears it by a quarter. A neglected wound scabs back, but never below half the progress reached. The mount fights back while wounded (`VesperWound`): it turns the wound away from a drainer standing at it, or answers with a bite, a tail sweep or a shake-off, each telegraphed. A full drain ruptures the wound and moves the health floor on; the third rupture starts the transition. Old saves with an exposed throne anchor load as an opened wound.
- **Puppet roster.** Vesper conducts seven shapes for the whole fight (`VesperPuppetRoster`): Veinwing Vulture, Marrow Spitter, Gorebound Hulk, Scarlet Mummer, Sanguine Hound, Cinder Bellows and Mnemonist Puppet. The Ringmaster Pattern is not his. A muster calls up to three of them (shapes never fielded first) on strings from his Crossbar (`PuppetStrings.descend`), with trial stats. His puppets hunt the ordeal owner while the owner is in the arena, turn back if they stray past it, and unspool a few seconds after their conductor is gone. A shape the player kills is struck for the rest of the fight; other deaths return it. Puppets that have been out for 20 seconds can be recalled to wait in the roster: he raises the Crossbar and casts three vein strings onto each one (`VesperRecallGeometry`, timed by `VesperRecallRules`). The strings hook its shoulders and draw taut for a second while it is slowed and ringed on the floor, which is the last chance to kill it and strike the shape. Then they haul it up and reel what is left of it into the Crossbar; ordeal resets and the end of phase 1 unspool any still out.
- **Phase 2, the Evening Star**, in three acts (`VesperEveningStarAct`, driven by `VesperEveningStarController`):
  - **Locked (100%-67%).** One weapon per stance for the full stance timer. Each weapon has a chained moveset of openers (some with a gap-closer), follow-ups and a finisher whose poses link (`VesperChainGraph`), so strings flow instead of resetting to idle; links within a string recover in 3 ticks, finishers fully. Between beats he casts one of his stance school's fight manipulations.
  - **Open (67%-33%).** A follow-up may hand the string to another school whose move starts in the same pose: his weapon and school morph mid-string. He casts authored cross-school synergy chains (`VesperSynergyChains`), such as Sanguine Magnetism into Synaptic Jolt or Glacial Grasp into Exsanguinate.
  - **Sickles (33%-0).** The dual Living Sickles run as strings (`VesperSickleRules`): Reaping (two to five alternating reaps), Hook & Reel (a catch stays on the line and reels the target into a reel-spin, a launching rise, or a pass-through cut from behind; a cancelled move lets the line go; a raised shield is ripped aside; enough damage or sprinting away snaps the tether and staggers him), Gallows Wheel (two tethers sweep around him at waist height), cyclone and pounce families with feints, crescent volleys (fans, staggers, low skimmers to jump, a crescent that returns), and Anchor Hook to slingshot out of corners. Spins speed up and bleed out and carry their momentum into the next move. Below 10%, once, he performs **Harvest** and then stands spent for three seconds.
  - Stance changes no longer freeze him: the morph plays over his next strike.
- **Manipulations.** `VesperManipulationCaster` lets him cast any fight manipulation. Those with a shared entity cast use it; the rest are Vesper-side boss versions that fire the manipulation's own authored visual form with a matching effect. Heals, summons, utilities, weapon conjures, extra-heart passives and death-cheats are excluded. Wills are unaffected. See the coverage table below.
- **Borrowed attacks.** Every roster shape the player failed to kill in phase 1 (still out, recalled, or never called) gives the Evening Star one borrowed attack (`VesperBorrowedAttacks`), flashed as puppet sigils at his awakening: the Hulk's thread yank into a slam, the Spitter's marrow volley and caustic pools, the Vulture's leap and dive, the Mummer's bursting decoys, the Hound's Blood Curs, the Bellows' ember breath, and the Mnemonist's lash replaying the biggest recent hit he took. They slot between strings, rarer in the Sickle act, each on a 15-second cooldown.
- **Render path.** The mount is generated (`tools/model_export/vesper_mount.py` + `vesper_mount_anim.java` -> `VesperMountModel`, `vesper_mount.png`): a new head and neck, six four-segment legs on a procedural tripod gait, grasping claw arms, a six-segment tail, a throne on a raised dais, scutes the Carapace Aneurysm blows off and regrows, and two pairs of translucent veined wings (`VesperMountWingMembraneLayer`). It is painted as an overgrown morphling, a blood organism grown over an insect. Its armour is overlapping scutes: umber-maroon plates stretched along each limb, with worn pale free margins and shadowed roots. The seams between them stay dark until the organism swells through them as raw, veined flesh. It has a ribbed pale underbelly, wet sinew joints and blood-washed bone. Only Vesper's throne keeps its lacquer. A large Hermit's bottle gourd is slung across the throne's back, and the shattered green morphling jar the organism grew out of sits at the throne's right rear, its tissue rooting into the throne and the thorax. Both clear the carapace wound. The wound plates are the model's own painted `wound_scute`, chitin outside and veined tissue underneath. Vesper himself keeps his Blockbench model, seated by `VesperRiderLayer` and posed in Java (`VesperRiderMotion`); only his transformation clip remains keyframed. The Evening Star's new moves are posed procedurally (`VesperEveningStarMotion`). Review everything with `./gradlew.bat runVesperReviewClient` (open the `VesperReview` save after startup).
- Implemented reward: `memory_of_vesper`, a rare fire-resistant material rendered as a pome-like memory with the Monolith Fragment shader. It is placed directly in an Iron Brazier and absorbed through Living Staff Blood Absorption; completion awakens Vesper's memory, upgrades the staff focus, and permanently grants the Mortem-aligned `conjure_sickle` form in the radial's interior ring.

**The Mycophant**
- The Spawn Mother: the hivemind's brood cultivator, mother of every Erythromycelium strain, and the Apotheos path's gate and key. She absorbs whoever transcends to breed new strains, and tends every life her infection made. Surviving her claim proves the player the hive's heir. A genderless brood-mother: motherly, never sexual or feminine ("she" in text).
- `tools/model_export/mycophant.py` bakes the [Spawn Mother Blockbench project](art/mycophant_spawn_mother/MycophantSpawnMother.bbmodel) into `MycophantMesh` at one texel per grid unit and 16 grid units per block. `MycophantModel` animates the rig from the existing encounter clocks. The painted gestation sac shares the base atlas with the body. `MycophantGlowLayer` lights the sensory pits, sacs, vents and siphon mouth, and `MycophantBroodLayer` carries the Fungling during the waking. At the split, the skull hinges apart, the pulp blooms and the hyphae wings unfurl.
- Fight: `MycophantController`, `MycophantMoves` and the pure `Mycophant*Rules` classes; see the Nursery section above. Focal effects use the Hemomancy suite (`BossTelegraphs`, HutosLib tendrils, `sendClawSlash`, `MycophantSiphonTetherGeometry`); there are no vanilla particles on her.
- Implemented reward: `mycophant_tendril`, a `VasculariumCharmItem` subclass that fits the Charm of Vascularium slot. Owned victories deliver it through the pending claim; the loot table `data/hemomancy/loot_table/entities/mycophant.json` drops it only from an unowned, direct-summoned Mycophant. While equipped it renders as the equipped charm stack and adds a full-body red/orange/yellow fungalization layer with a mushroom-head replacement (`FungalHeadAttachmentModel`, kept from the first-attempt Morphling art under a neutral name; it is not a Morphling strain).
- Review: `./gradlew.bat runMycophantReviewClient` (see `docs/TESTING.md`).

**Implementation anchors:** `EntityInit` registers all three entity types and attributes; `client/registry/EntityRendererRegistrar` registers renderers; `EndgameBossActions` contains the shared combat helpers; `EndgameBossCombatRules` contains the tested cadence/threshold rules; `EndgameBossMusicHandler` handles client-side looping music.

### 5.11 Boss Presentation: Bar Frames and Openings

Every boss bar is drawn in a frame of its own instead of the plain vanilla bar. The frame unfurls when the bar appears,
keeps a lit chip of the health just lost before it drains, marks the boss's phase thresholds with notches, and changes
look when the boss changes phase (the Mycophant's collar parts when she joins, Vesper's scutes crack at each wound, the
Naeglerophaeon's arcs recolour with its stage, Hemorath's iron tarnishes as the vessel empties).

| Boss | Opening |
|---|---|
| The Mycophant | The waking in the Nursery under a letterbox, her name over the roar; the rematch is a short shot round her turn. |
| Annetta Knowles | Harbinger route: a 3-second shot from over her shoulder to her face as she arms herself; untouchable meanwhile. |
| The Stained Priestess | A low shot at the pool rising with her, her name on the scream. |
| The Latent Infection | The player's own view while Annetta drinks, then a shot of the tear; its name once it stands. |
| Naeglerophaeon | 3.5 seconds gathering out of its synaptic node, untouchable, before it hunts. |
| Vesper, the Crowned Refusal | A 4-second arrival: a long look down the arena, then the mount rears; untouchable meanwhile. |
| The Saints | A 3-second rise out of the broken sarcophagus, untouchable, the bar shown once it stands. |
| Phlegethosoma | The fluke rearing out of the ichor, the camera low on the surface and climbing with the head; the name lands at the top of the rear (`PhlegethosomaScene`, `PhlegethosomaCombatRules.INTRO_TICKS`). |
| The Bloom Warden | Uprooting: the camera rises from the tier floor with it as it stands out of its moss; the name lands as the fronds open (`BloomWardenScene`). |
| The Kindled Champion | Stepping out of the elders: the camera comes round its flank and climbs its neck to the flaring crown (`KindledChampionScene`). |
| Hydra | Not fought. Its largest head rises for the player the Head-tender called it for, and the view hands back looking up as the crown comes down (`HydraRiseScene`). |
| The Circus Ringmaster | The camera tilts up from the sawdust to find him in the rafters and pulls back over the big top as the first knife falls; the finale's hidden crossing into his Chamber happens under it (`CircusRingmasterScene`; see [CIRCUS.md](CIRCUS.md)). |

Phase changes get a short card (letterbox and name, no camera): Annetta breaking, the Mycophant joining, the
Naeglerophaeon conducting, Vesper unbecoming in the cocoon and named the Evening Star as it bursts, and Hemorath's
vessel emptying. Holding Sneak for a second skips a scene's presentation; the player stays held only while the server
still binds them (the Mycophant waking before control returns). The client config's `boss_presentation` section
turns off the frames, the cinematic camera or the shake. A reconnect respawn never replays an opening, a reload
mid-opening carries on where it was, and a Mycophant rematch plays only its short form.

## 6. The Unstained Path (Anti-Hemomancy)

The divergent/opposing path. The player abandons blood magic in pursuit of purification and enlightenment, guided by **Unstained Zealot** NPCs and the silent patronage of **Our Lady of Still Waters**.

### 6.1 Our Lady of Still Waters — Patron of the Unstained

The Unstained revere a mysterious figure known only as **Our Lady of Still Waters** (sometimes whispered as *"The Lady of the Forgotten Waters"* or *"She Who Absolves"*). She is described in Unstained scripture as:

- A **tall woman** with **white hair** that cascades like flowing water
- Clad in **white robes** that shimmer faintly with silver thread
- Eyes of **liquid silver** that see through all deception and corruption
- Skin of **pale blue**, as though touched by the still waters

Her origins are unknown — some Unstained texts suggest she is a being from before the fungal infection that birthed hemomancy, a guardian spirit of purity who was driven into hiding when blood magic first took root. Others believe she is a manifestation of the world's immune response to the alien fungus, a living antibody in humanoid form.

**Connection to the Lethean Poppies:**
The **Lethean Poppies** that grow across the world are said to bloom wherever Our Lady once walked. The dew they produce — **Lethean Dew** — carries her essence: the power of forgetting. Just as the mythological River Lethe washed away memories, the lethean poppies help players *forget* their blood manipulations, severing the ties that bind them to hemomancy. The Unstained believe that harvesting and refining these poppies is a sacred act of devotion to their patron.

**Tears of Silthmere** are distilled from Lethean Dew at an Altar of Cleansing, concentrating Our Lady's blessing into a single potent draught. When offered at her altar, these tears trigger a one-time purification from the Lady herself.

**The Pallid Icon** began as a historically unique devotional relic recovered from the bottom of a forgotten river. Later Unstained reproduced its posture as consecrated copies, which is why the ordinary item can exist more than once. The game does not distinguish the original with a separate item, tag, or stronger mechanic; the distinction is historical lore only.

### 6.2 Unstained NPC Dialogue System

Two Unstained NPC types guide the player through the purification journey. All dialogue trees are fully implemented.

**Unstained Zealot** (`ZealotDialogueTrees`) — recruiter; the NPC who first offers the path.

| Player State | Dialogue Branch |
|---|---|
| No blood at all | Dismisses gently: "You bear no mark of the crimson arts." |
| Active blood, Degree 0-1 | Full plea with concerned sadness: the Church treats early infection as something that can still be healed |
| Active blood, Degree 2-4 | Full plea with increasing caution: the Zealot still offers help, but questions the player's motives and attachment to the Covenant |
| Active blood, Degree 5 (Illuminatus) | Full plea with hesitant disdain: aid is still offered, but the Church assumes the request may be manipulation or regret arriving late |
| Active blood, Degree 6+, no founded bloodline | Full plea with late-arrival suspicion: the cure is still open, but the Zealot asks why the player waited so long |
| Active blood, founded bloodline (not severed) | Refuses the cure (`bloodlineFounded`): the founder's blood runs through other people, so ordinary rites cannot reach it while the covenant stands. Degree alone never triggers this |
| Active blood, any Degree (plea) | Explains the hemolytic rites, offers craft-hemolytic info branch, `zealot_accept_purification` / `zealot_accept_church` / `zealot_reject_help` outcomes |
| Already on purification path — Corrupted | "Continue your work at the podium, and the stain shall lift." |
| Purity 25–49 (Tainted) | Verdigris Aura info branch |
| Purity 50–74 (Cleansing) | Altar of Cleansing info branch |
| Purity 75–99 (Absolved) | Clarity Rite info branch |
| Clarity unlocked | Silver Ward info branch |
| Enlightened | Final reverence: the journey complete |

**Unstained Acolyte** (`AcolyteDialogueTrees`) — found at Unstained temples; provides stage-aware guidance and tasks.

| Stage | Dialogue Content |
|---|---|
| Not on path | Gentle introduction to the Unstained way; "Who are you?" branch |
| Corrupted (0–24) | Explains how to purify; gives task: gather Ghost Pipe (`acolyte_task_gather_ghost_pipe`) |
| Tainted (25–49) | **Our Lady of Still Waters lore** (3 lines about the Lady's nature); tasks: wreath offering / hemolytic offering |
| Cleansing (50–74) | **Silver Veil lore** (inner layer of purity shielding the soul); task: consecration |
| Absolved (75–99) | Explains the Clarity path (3-line clarity branch) |
| Purified (100, pre-Clarity) | Explains how to unlock Clarity |
| Clarity phase | Silver Ward lore; task: chalice offering (`acolyte_task_chalice`) |
| Enlightened | Ultimate reverence: "The Lady weeps for joy." |

### 6.3 Entry Requirements

- Standard path: the player claims a Blood Temple heart, attaches the Charm of Vascularium to activate blood control, then later finds an Unstained Church seeking cure or healing
- Unstained Zealots can offer ordinary purification at any Harbinger degree until the player actually founds a bloodline. Degree alone never closes the route.
- Founding a bloodline closes ordinary cure because the founder has integrated the infection into other lives. A founder cannot use Annetta's Unstained purification route; defeating the infection unleashed by her fatal Harbinger encounter unlocks the exceptional Severed Covenant rite. Completing it disbands the founder's bloodline and reopens cure.
- The Zealot directs the player to suppress the infection with **Hemolytic Solution** at an **Unstained Podium**, then perform the **Rite of Lethean Baptism**.

### 6.4 Phase 1: Purity (0–100)

Prepared by using Hemolytic Solution at the Unstained Podium, then initiated by the Rite of Lethean Baptism:
- The podium records that the infection is suppressed; it does not itself begin Purity.
- The first successful Baptism sets `begunPurification = true`, and sets starting purity from `UnstainedAccessRules.baptismStartingPurity`: 50 minus 10 per Harbinger Degree, never below 0 (Degree 0 = 50, Degree 1 = 40, Degree 5 and higher = 0). A founder who completed the Severed Covenant always starts at 0. The canonical Absolution Dagger comes later, from the Rite of Clarity Ascension (the Guardian replaces a lost one).

As purity rises, blood magic becomes increasingly penalized:

| Stage | Purity ≥ | Blood Magic Penalty |
|-------|----------|---------------------|
| Corrupted | 0 | None (1.0× cost) |
| Tainted | 25 | +10% cost (1.10×) |
| Cleansing | 50 | +25% cost (1.25×) |
| Absolved | 75 | +50% cost (1.50×) |
| Purified | 100 | **Completely blocked** |

- **Verdigris Aura** is the early defense and scales linearly with `purity / 100`.

#### Purity Sources

**Combat:**

| Source | Purity Gained | Condition |
|--------|---------------|-----------|
| **Killing a Hemomancy mob** | +0.75 | Any entity tagged `hemomancy_mob` |
| **Killing an Undead mob** | +0.25 | Any MobType.UNDEAD (zombies, skeletons, phantoms, etc.) |
| **Killing a Hostile mob** | +0.10 | Any other MobCategory.MONSTER |
| **Flawless kill bonus** | +0.25 extra | Added to any kill reward if player hasn't taken damage in last 5 seconds |

**Survival & Exploration:**

| Source | Purity Gained | Condition |
|--------|---------------|-----------|
| **Hemolytic Solution on Podium** | 0 | One-time infection suppression required before Lethean Baptism |
| **Tears of Silthmere on Altar of Cleansing** | +25.0 | One-time blessing from Our Lady of Still Waters |
| **Lethean Poppy Wreath on Altar** | +5.0 | Repeatable offering at the Altar of Cleansing |
| **Completing an Advancement** | +1.5 | Any advancement (boss kills, exploration, progression) |
| **Picking up XP orbs** | +0.1 | Requires active **Hemolysis** effect |
| **Sleeping through the night** | +5.0 | Requires active **Hemolysis** effect; natural wake only |
| **Hemolysis effect tick** | +0.01/tick | Passive gain while Hemolysis is active (very slow) |

**Farming & Mercy:**

| Source | Purity Gained | Condition |
|--------|---------------|-----------|
| **Breeding animals** | +0.75 | Creating life — any successful breeding |
| **Planting crops/saplings/flowers** | +0.10 | Placing a block tagged as crop, sapling, or flower |
| **Healing a tamed animal** | +1.0 | When a tamed pet heals (feeding a wolf, etc.) |
| **Natural self-healing (no blood)** | +0.1 | Healing 1+ heart with blood volume empty or inactive |

**Restraint & Discipline:**

| Source | Purity Gained | Condition |
|--------|---------------|-----------|
| **Blood magic abstinence** | +1.0 | Every 5 minutes without using any blood manipulation |
| **Empty blood renunciation** | +0.30 | Once a minute (`EMPTY_BLOOD_REWARD_COOLDOWN_TICKS` 1,200) while blood volume is zero or inactive (abandoned hemomancy) |

*Kill rewards are not gated by Hemolysis — any player on the Unstained path earns purity from kills. XP and sleep rewards require the Hemolysis effect. Abstinence timer resets whenever a blood manipulation is used. `UnstainedPacingRules` paces the small rewards: XP pickup at most once per 100 ticks, planting once per 200, a tamed pet's heal once per 600.*

### 6.5 Phase 2: Clarity (0–100)

Prepared after reaching Purified (purity = 100) by using **Consecrated Copper** at the Unstained Podium, then unlocked by the **Rite of Clarity Ascension**:
- The podium records clarity preparation; it does not itself unlock Clarity.
- The rite sets `clarityUnlocked = true`. Blood magic is already gone by then: the first Rite of the Closed Vein at Purified strips it (`PathMutualExclusionHelper.completeUnstainedCure`).

| Stage | Clarity ≥ |
|-------|-----------|
| Awakened | 0 |
| Discerning | 25 |
| Vigilant | 50 |
| Resolute | 75 |
| Enlightened | 100 |

- **Silver Ward** is the advanced defense and scales linearly with `clarity / 100`.
- Clarity gradually changes preserved biology. With `c = clamp(clarity, 0, 100) / 100`:
  - Instant Health and potion Regeneration healing are multiplied by `1 - 0.75c` (25% response at Enlightened).
  - Poison damage is multiplied by `1 - 0.75c` (25% damage at Enlightened).
  - Food exhaustion is multiplied by `1 - 0.65c` (35% exhaustion at Enlightened).
- These modifiers require `clarityUnlocked`; Purity alone does not alter food, poison, Regeneration, or healing-potion mechanics. Unrelated healing and damage sources are unchanged.
- Reaching 100 clarity = **Enlightenment**, the final state

### 6.6 Unstained Progression Level (`ProgressionGates.unstainedStage`)

To gate Unstained cardinal rites the same way Harbinger degree gates Harbinger rites, the full purity → clarity path is divided into **8 numbered levels** by `ProgressionGates.unstainedStage(Player)`:

| Level | Milestone | Condition |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| 0 | Not begun | `!hasBegunPurification()` |
| 1 | Begun | `hasBegunPurification()`, purity < 25 |
| 2 | Tainted | purity ≥ 25 |
| 3 | Cleansing | purity ≥ 50 |
| 4 | Absolved | purity ≥ 75 |
| 5 | Purified | `isPurified()` (purity ≥ 100) |
| 6 | Discerning | clarity ≥ 25 |
| 7 | Vigilant | clarity ≥ 50 |
| 8 | Enlightened | `isEnlightened()` (clarity ≥ 100) |

These levels are compared against each Unstained recipe's explicit `required_degree` value through `RecipeDegreeGates`. The field intentionally mirrors Harbinger degree gates for shared tooling, but Unstained recipes are cataloged separately from Harbinger Blood Structure and Cardinal Rite recipes in §15.

### 6.7 Fully Purified Biological Traits — Implementation Boundary

The lore sheet's Fully Purified traits remain canonical direction, but they are not all runtime claims. Current implementation status is:

| Trait | Runtime status |
|---|---|
| Permanent blood-magic lockout after Clarity | **Implemented** — the first Rite of the Closed Vein at Purified deactivates blood and strips remaining Harbinger progression. |
| Reduced potion healing, poison damage, and food exhaustion as Clarity rises | **Implemented** — these are the current gradual biological changes described in §6.5. |
| Coma/bloodless transition and awakening | **Planned / narrative only** — no discrete runtime transition handler. |
| Halted normal aging | **Canonical lore only** — Minecraft has no ordinary player-aging system to alter. |
| Illness-sensing presence | **Planned** — no dedicated detection mechanic. |
| Healing touch | **Planned** — no Fully Purified touch-heal mechanic. |
| Passive plant growth | **Planned** — no Fully Purified growth aura. |

Do not present the planned traits as current player powers until their handlers, feedback, and progression gates exist.

---

## 7. Mutual Exclusion of Paths

The two paths are **mutually exclusive**. Resets are handled by `PathMutualExclusionHelper`:
- **Beginning Purity** (Lethean Baptism after podium suppression) starts the escalating blood-magic penalties; Harbinger progression is not stripped until the first Rite of the Closed Vein at Purified
- **Completing a Harbinger degree rite** → resets all Unstained progress (purity → 0, clarity → 0, clarityUnlocked → false, begunPurification → false, **all KnownStillArts cleared**)
- **The cure** happens at the first Rite of the Closed Vein at Purified, before Clarity Ascension; `enforceHarbingerResetOnClarity()` is only reachable from `/hemo unstained`
- Message: *"Your purification has been undone by the blood rite."* / *"The Hematic Order falls silent within you."*

The runtime gates are phase-specific rather than one immediate blanket lockout:

| Unstained phase | May gain Harbinger progression | May use known blood powers | Harbinger progression gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outsider / Novitiate | Yes | Yes | Open |
| Purifying / Cure Ready | No | Yes | Blocked |
| Cleansed Unpledged / Pledged | No | No | Blocked |

This is why beginning purification does not erase an existing loadout, while completing Clarity does. The purification rites themselves retain their explicit exception routes so the player can finish the path they began.

---

## 8. Blood Manipulations

### 8.0 The two verbs and Sculptings (core-loop Track 1)

**Verbs.** Projection pushes blood into the world and Absorption draws it back. The active verb is player state, chosen
with the verb key (see the dated note at the top). `VerbChannel` says which verb a player is channelling: a cell hand is
its verb, the Living Staff carries the active verb (never while threading an engram).

**Targets.** `VerbTargeting.pick` is the one pick for the server chain and the hand's stream. A Sculpting declares the
kinds it wants: `BLOCK`, `FLUID` (a fluid in its own right; without it a fluid surface reads as its block, as plain
Projection always aimed), `CREATURE` (aimed along the look ray, in front of the block), `ITEMS` (the item entity the aim
finds plus the items within 1.25 blocks, at most 16) and `AIR` (the point at full reach when nothing stood in the way).
The nearest wanted thing wins; on a tie a creature beats items beat a fluid beat a block.

**Sculptings.** A `VerbSculpting` declares `wants`, `claims(player, target)` (decidable on both sides), `pulse`, optional
`begin` / `end`, its `cadence` (default 10 ticks), its `bloodPerPulse`, whether it `roots` the player (by Absorption's
movement rules and skills) and a `reachScale` (0.25 to 3). `SculptingDispatcher` alone reads Sculptings and names no
manipulation (`SculptingGuardrailTest`). Chain order:

- Projection: founder initiation, Saint router, faltering Will, Cardinal Rite, **Sculpting if it claims**, block
  endpoints (Earthen Vein, Bloodwood), Blood Structure feed, Sanguine Condenser, infusion, `ProjectedBloodSink`.
- Absorption (hand and Staff): Vesper, Saint router, rite cancellation, block endpoints and reservoirs, faltering Will,
  **Sculpting if it claims** (before the full-body stop), then the living-target pulse.

A Sculpting that claims acts ahead of machines and reservoirs (CL-4); one that does not claim falls through, so the verb
behaves exactly as with nothing selected. While a claimed Sculpting works, its rooting replaces the verb's.

**Payment.** Each due pulse calls `BloodManipulation.tryPerformVerbPulse`: the cast key's possession and Unstained
refusals, paralysis, an absorbed family form, a dead
vein section, Unstained purity, the ninth-pome power lock, an active volume and the temper alignment gate, then the
Sculpting's own `admits` check (core-loop Track 9: a ward, a rite space or protected ground refuses here, before any
blood or Temper is priced; the claim holds, so the plain verb does not run; since round two Lignum Mortis, Lode Draw,
Pyretic Forge on a block, Hematic Hewing on the struck block and Vital Effusion check the player's right to change the
target here too, and say "That ground is not yours to change."), then the cost ledger's multiplier on `bloodPerPulse`, paid in full through `BloodAccounting.payUpkeep` as source `sculpting`
(counts as spend). The pulse runs inside the manipulation's school (`SchoolDamage.cast`). A pulse starts no cooldown and
sends no cooldown packet. Every 80 ticks of paid work counts as one ordinary use (mastery, temper shift, vascular strain,
skill points), so the D5 strain gate fills at about the rate of recasting. The Staff's rate skills raise the work a
pulse does (`SculptingPulse.workScale`), never its price. A refused pulse keeps the claim and retries on the next cadence
tick.

**Sessions.** `SculptingSessions` (session map, cleared through `TransientServerStateEvents`) holds one session per player:
the same manipulation, verb and target key, seen every tick. It opens on its first paid pulse: the Sculpting's `begin`
runs once the blood is paid and before that pulse works, and the manipulation's sustained cast presentation starts
through `CastingAnimationManager.channelStart` (the sustained cue holds while the Sculpting works, whatever the
manipulation's cast type). It ends when the use stops, the target or selection changes, or the claim lapses. The
presentation belongs to the channel, not the target: moving to a new target ends the Sculpting's work on the old one
(`end`) but keeps the presentation running, and a refused pulse stops it until a pulse is paid again.

**Feedback.** The `verb_channel` HUD layer (`VerbChannelOverlay`) shows the verb beside the crosshair while a verb is
channelled; with a Sculpting selected it adds the memory's icon, name and base mL/s, and four short ticks round the
crosshair that brighten when the Sculpting claims what is aimed at. The local player's hand stream lands on the claimed
target (`CellHandParticleEffects` asks `SculptingDispatcher.currentClaim`); other players' verbs and selections are not
synced, so their streams follow the plain pick.

**Left out on purpose.** Chamber visits do not snapshot the active verb: it is a preference, not inventory. Temper (the
spendable pool) is not charged by a pulse yet; core-loop Track 4 adds that charge in `tryPerformVerbPulse`.

### 8.0.1 The first Sculptings (core-loop Track 2)

**Round two P11 additions.** A refused pulse tells its owner's verb HUD (`VerbRefusalPacket`, the Sculpting's cadence plus
4 ticks): the reticle is barred in bone and the price line reads "Refused". Pyretic Forge plays no outpouring
(`presentsCast` false); its look is a heat tendril from the hand each pulse and the Forge cue at 0.45 size sunk 0.14
blocks under the items it works (0.8 above a fired block), with ember licks off the rim. Another player's client draws
a caster's stream where it lands: `VerbPresence` sends trackers both verbs' reach, the active verb and the selected
manipulation while a verb is channelled (`PacketSyncVerbPresence`, protocol 49), read through `ClientBridge` by
`VerbReach.of`, `SculptingDispatcher.selectedManipulation` and `VerbChannel.activeVerb`.

Every Sculpting is a factory in `common/manipulation/verb/Sculptings`, attached once in `ManipulationInit`; Sculptings are
for players only (no entity cast or Drudge action reaches one, `SculptingGuardrailTest`). A memory that sculpts a verb
says so on its tooltip (`tooltip.hemomancy.blood_memory.sculpting`, one line per verb, from
`hemomancy.manipulation.<id>.sculpting.<verb>`) and in its Liber page, on a line beginning "Sculpting,".

**Boss binding limit (LP-16, built 2026-11-14).** Both Blood Binding forms bind a boss through one gate
(`BloodBindingManip.applyBinding`, `BossBindings`, `BossBindingRules`). A boss takes max health / 100 successful bindings
(at least 1: the Wither 3, the Warden 5), one count saved on the boss entity (`hemomancy:boss_bindings_taken`) and
shared by every player; it never comes back on the same body, so a Saint that returns to its tomb wakes with a fresh
count (NQ-04-2). Each attempt slips by max health / 2,000, held between 10% and 60%, times 0.5 + 0.5 x the boss's
health fraction: a 1,000 HP boss at full health slips half the time (NQ-04-3). A slip costs the blood, starts the R
cast's cooldown and does not count; the held form then waits 60 ticks before trying that boss again. One binding is one
hold of the boss length; it drops when it ends, whatever the player holds, and the next hold is a new attempt
(NQ-04-1). The constricted slow and the Animus brand land on a boss only with a binding that held (NQ-04-4); the Blood
Lash charged crack is left alone. The binder reads "The binding slips off ..." or "... will not be bound again."

**Narrow Sculptings (round two P4).** A manipulation may carry narrow Sculptings of a verb ahead of its main one:
`addProjectionSculpting(Sculptings::x)` / `addAbsorptionSculpting(Sculptings::x)` beside `setProjectionSculpting`. The dispatcher
tries them in claim order (narrow ones in the order attached, then the main one), after a held channel already open
keeps the channel: so with Glacial Grasp selected, open water freezes, a creature the caster may harm takes the ice
hand (8.0.2), and a hand already out keeps its creature when the aim crosses water. `SculptingDispatcher.selected` still names the main Sculpting (the HUD default,
the channel's movement); the channel HUD prices the Sculpting that actually claims the aim.

**The second wave (round two P4).** Seven memories took a Sculpting; each keeps its R cast. Every block they change is
the player's edit (`PlayerBlockEdits`), refused before any blood where the player may not build. Furnace Veins burns
blood as fuel only while held (nothing is banked: the furnace's own burn time is raised to one pulse and 5 ticks,
through the `FurnaceFuelAccessor` mixin). Frozen Cruor from a Sculpting remembers whether it froze a water source
(`TemporaryIceSavedData` key `water`) and melts back to it. Since 2026-11-15 every Frozen Cruor does, whoever laid it: R casts, Wills, Vesper and Drudges too (NQ-05-13). Carrion Communion fills Mortem
Temper through `TemperCharge.fillFromCarrion` and never gives blood: the dead hold no living blood. Ferric Rampart's
swept wall is `FerricConstructShapes.Kind.SEGMENT` (one wide, three tall, `.375` deep, appended after `SPIKE`), a wall in
every way (`Kind.isWall`). Campfires and candles switch through one helper, `SwitchableLights`, shared with the hot
gouge run and Blood Eclipse's snuff. A right click with a blood hand or the Staff on a block the selected Sculpting
claims channels the verb rather than opening the block (a furnace's or an anvil's screen;
`BloodProjectionInteractionEvents`). Glacial Grasp's freeze claims Frozen Cruor only while open water lies beside it;
dry ice is the plant's. Taught on the Liber pages Mending, Fire and the Dead and Ice and Iron Walls.

Bosses take half the constricted tail. `ManipulationCombatHelper.canHarm(player, target)` decides who may be bound; a
surrogate on a Qliphoth grand floor is held without end, as by the R cast. Blood per second is the base price before
the cost ledger's multipliers; a pulse pays it through `BloodManipulation.tryPerformVerbPulse` as described in 8.0.
Work toward a credited use now belongs to the channel, like the cast presentation: a target change keeps it, so a haul
or a sweep that changes target every tick still earns uses.

**Lignum Mortis.** `CrawlSession` (verb package) is the shared crawl: a selector, a budget and a dismantle that breaks
through `PlayerBlockEdits.breakBlock` with a bare hand; the R channel uses the same crawl. The Sculpting's crawl (a
session map in `LignumMortisSculpting`) begins on the struck block; aiming at another block of the same crawl, or one
touching it, keeps the crawl going. Letting go fells what it reached; a crawl that has reached everything fells at once.
A crawl the player has looked away from waits 40 ticks for them to come back or let go (letting go fells), then lapses.

**Pyretic Forge.** Items are smelted by the vanilla smelting recipes (nothing authored twice), dropped where the stack
lay, with the furnace's experience as orbs. Blocks go through the infusion recipe type with two optional keys:
`"sculpting": "hemomancy:pyretic_forge"` (only that Sculpting runs the recipe; plain infusion ignores it) and
`"in_place": true` (convert where it stands through `PlayerBlockEdits.replace`; without it the block is lifted and drops
the result). Twelve recipes live in `data/hemomancy/recipe/pyretic_forge/`. The block shows the infusion veins while it
heats and the Forge's molten heart on its top when it fires. Ores are not fired; mine them and smelt what drops.

**Tendon Line.** The anchor lives on the player (`hemomancy:tendon_anchor`, `TendonAnchor`, transient: never saved, not
kept through death, dropped on a dimension change), synced to the owner and the players tracking them by
`PacketSyncTendonAnchor` (which names the owner's entity) through the `PlayerStateSync` entry `TENDON_ANCHOR`, and to a
player who starts tracking a rooted owner. The haul claims whenever a line is rooted in the player's dimension, so with
the Tendon Line selected and no line rooted, plain Absorption runs. It snaps when the player strays past 4/3 of the
throw reach, when the anchored face can no longer hold it, or on arrival (within 1.35 blocks). A haul is not flight
(`FlightArbiter` is not involved). `TendonLineRenderer` draws every rooted line in the dimension within 96 blocks (round
two P11) from the drawn palm (`CellHandStreams.palm`): a soft sheath, a living-blood ribbon 0.10 blocks wide at the hand
and 0.07 at the root, a pale seam and one sinew wound along the whole length, with a clot where it is rooted. Slack, it
sags 0.22 blocks and throbs slowly; hauled, it pulls straight and throbs faster. The cell hand pours no ordinary stream
while the line claims (`VerbSculpting.drawsOwnStream`). R says the line has nothing to cast and costs nothing.

**Blood Binding.** Each pulse holds every creature the binding reaches for one cadence plus 6 ticks and constricts it
for the tail beyond that; a longer binding already on a creature (an R cast) is left alone. Each pulse resends the same
binding tendril seed, and the client extends a running tendril instead of regrowing it.

**Brazier transmutation.** `BrazierTransmutationRite` is the fourth `BrazierRite`, tried after Memory, Scar and Living
Weapon Graft, and it accepts only offerings none of them accepts. It keeps the shared lifecycle: insertion, Projection
to light, held Absorption through the 60-tick channel, sneak to retrieve. The recipe type
`hemomancy:brazier_transmutation` has `input`, optional `sculpting` (the manipulation that must be selected and equipped;
without it any selection or none), optional `catalyst` (held in the off hand) with optional `catalyst_count` (how many
the off hand must hold, default 1; all are spent), `blood_cost` (paid on
completion, source `brazier_transmutation`), `result` and optional `byproduct`. A recipe naming the selection wins over
one naming none; with Pyretic Forge selected and no recipe, the offering is smelted by its vanilla recipe for 15 mL. The
result goes to the inventory (or drops at the bowl), the offering is consumed and the fire goes out. The twelve
recipes: charcoal (two from a log), glass (two from sand), leather (rotten flesh) and hematic iron scrap (hematic iron
powder, with coal or charcoal in the off hand) and flint (two from gravel) under Pyretic Forge; packed ice (from ice,
with 3 more ice in the off hand, 30 mL), blue ice (from packed ice, with 3 more packed ice, 60 mL) and obsidian (from a
magma block) under Glacial Grasp; rooted dirt, moss (from stone), an oak sapling (from a dead bush) and bone meal with
ruinous spores (from a bone) under Vital Effusion (CQ-5, CB-18, NQ-01-12, NQ-01-13, built 2026-11-15). Every recipe
names a Sculpting now; the field stays optional. Each has a JEI row
(`BrazierTransmutationRecipeCategory`); Pyretic Forge's block recipes show in the Blood Infusion category with the
memory to select.

Blood manipulations are abilities fueled by blood. Lore-wise, they are dormant memories everyone has access to. They can now be learned through two paths: crude memory shards for early, weak starter echoes, and full **Blood Memory** items for the refined midgame-and-later memory-weaving path.

### September 2026 casting corrections

The [acquisition pass](archive/done/manipulation_work_plan/03-acquisition-results.md) verifies all eleven manipulation families, keeps loaded crossbow ammunition through staff restoration/reload, and gives a physical Thread Ripper memory if Liberation's direct grant is rejected. Base cast, upkeep, reactive and staff-switch prices are distinguished in the existing UI; item attack costs remain separate. The [90-recipe ledger](archive/done/manipulation_work_plan/03-memory-recipe-ledger.md) includes blank and lantern costs. Final repricing awaits combat tuning; survival acquisition and full graft/reward routes retain live acceptance checks.

[Work area 2 results](archive/done/manipulation_work_plan/02-targeting-and-casting-results.md) records M08–M12's targeting, payment and passive rules. Aimed rays stop at collision geometry; nearest-victim powers require visibility but still search around the caster. The audited hostile payloads exclude allies, owned/allied summons and PvP-disabled players. Existing area pulses retain their area geometry. Circuit requires allied recipients; Suture falls back to self. Predictable invalid actions validate before blood/cooldown/mastery bookkeeping; exact-cost payment is allowed without a hidden 1 mL reserve. Blackhearted, Sovereign and Phoenix require active blood, an enabled equipped passive and their registered alignment; Sovereign reuses the command manager for five seconds of redirection.

The 9 September presentation pass extends that work with a shared formation, established-state, and dissolution lifecycle for manipulation visuals. Physical schools gather visible blood into the final material, persistent effects refresh rather than restart, and explicit stops or lost sources dissolve without resurrecting stale cues. School bodies and boundary rings remain visible on Minimal particles; secondary motes obey the existing particle cap and distance settings. Lux/Tenebris, Flammeus/Congeatio, Animus/Mortem, and Ferric/Ductilis now have distinct shader-backed material languages while keeping gameplay geometry, server authority, and exact range indicators separate from cosmetics.

### 8.0.2 Strands (core-loop Track 12)

A strand is a `StrandSculpting` (package `common/manipulation/verb/strand/`) built from data: a `Sculptings` factory calls
`Strands.lash(...)` with a `StrandSpec` (form, blood per pulse, damage scale, the accent's long state duration, the
snap's price) and a `LashProfile`, and `ManipulationInit` attaches it with `setProjectionSculpting`. Since 2026-11-12
only `Strands.lash` is on a memory: Blood Lash, Searing Lash and Gloam Laceration. `Strands.jet`, `spray`, `plant` and
`brand` stay in the code and no memory uses them; they and the stain run stay for tests while blood on the ground
waits (CQ-25). Long Strand, Whipcrack and Free Hand also train the eight held manipulations (CQ-20 B), and Second
Strand is the lash twin only (CQ-22 A); both are below.
Nothing in the strand package names a manipulation (`SculptingGuardrailTest`); a strand's school is its manipulation's.
`StrandService` runs every open strand: `begin` on the first paid pulse, `hold` every tick, `pulse` on the cadence (10
ticks), `end` on release. A strand is a **held channel** (`VerbSculpting.holdsChannel`): the dispatcher keeps it whatever
the aim crosses until the use stops or a pulse is refused, then lets go. Rites, Saints and Wills still claim first every
tick. Blocks that take blood (`StrandSculpting.takesBlood`: a blood endpoint, a reservoir, a projected-blood sink or a
cauldron) are never claimed, so a station fills as before with a strand selected.

| Memory | Form | Blood per second | Pace | Reach | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Blood Lash (new) | Lash | 15 | 0.8 | verb + 2 | The teaching lash: 0.6 times the lash's damage; even between tap and charge |
| Searing Lash | Lash | 60 | 0.8 | verb + 2 | Sweeps 3 to 6 by tip speed; the crack 9 with a long Searing; leans on the charge (up to x 1.75) |
| Gloam Laceration (P5) | Lash | 40 | 0.8 | verb + 2 | 0.85 times the lash; its crack lays a long Obscured; leans on the tap, whose third blow in a row lays a short one |

Conjuration and Ferric Spikes were in this table as jets, sprays and plants until 2026-11-12. They are not strands
now. What each does is in the next two tables.

**Held manipulations that are not strands (2026-11-12).** Four memories whose strand form contradicted their name were

the channel.

A charge under 25% buys no hold or fire. Ambush and tails apply to cracks and taps, not to sweeps.

After this no registered memory uses the jet, spray, plant or brand kits; only the three lashes are strands. The kits stay
in the code, exercised by their tests on lent memories. Second Strand adds only the twin lash (CQ-22 A), and Taut Line's
jet half and Deep Brand's set-speed half are dropped from the skills (CQ-20 B).

**The skills on the eight held manipulations (CQ-20 B, built 2026-11-15).** `HeldSkills` gives the eight above the
lash's own numbers: Long Strand scales their reach (`reachScale(Player)`, and Hematic Flare's beam and Glacial Grasp's
leash with it), Whipcrack their attack-button hit (damage x1.15 and the hit's school state x1.2 a level: the dome's
flash, the ice hand's squeeze, the beam's flash, the flame flare, a clicked lance needle, and how long Ferric Spikes'
standing blades stay, which deal no hit of their own), and Free Hand their own pace (+0.1 a level, never past
walking). Synaptic Jolt sets no pace and Cruor Javelin and Synaptic Jolt take no accent, so only Long Strand reaches
them.

**Cut on 2026-11-12 (owner ruling: a held manipulation is not bound to one of the shared shapes, and none may be a recolour of another).** Blood Needle Fan, Prismatic Reproof, Hemorrhage, Conductive Mark, Insatiable Hunger and Grave Debt no longer shape held Projection: each only repeated its own R cast in a shared form. They cast on R as before. No memory holds a brand strand now; a brand is laid only by Blood Binding, and the brand kit (`BrandRules`, `StrandForm.BRAND`) stays in the code unused for a manipulation that earns it. Deep Brand's faster setting is dropped from the skill (CQ-20 B); its longer hold applies to a binding's brand (30, 45, 60 seconds). Text elsewhere in this document that names those six as strands is historical.

**The lash** (`LashRules`, pure, the same arithmetic on server and client; rebuilt 2026-11-12) has two halves. **The
tap**: a left click with a lash selected on a held Projection tool, nothing channelled and the crosshair on air or a
creature (`LashTapPacket`, `StrandService.tap`) strikes the first body on a straight line from the hand to the lash's
length, for the profile's tap blood (source `lash_tap`) and cooldown; it wounds only, unless the profile gives the tap a
state. A click on a block still mines. **The charged whip**: held Projection runs four phases. `CHARGING`: nothing is
out, an orb gathers in the hand, and the charge climbs to full over the profile's charge ticks at the profile's charge
blood. `THROWING`: a flick (the mouse turning 6 degrees or more in a tick, read by the casting client and sent in
`LashAimPacket`; the server reads none from the look) throws the lash over 4 ticks across a 60-degree arc centred on
the old aim, from the side opposite the flick; it cracks on the first body or block it meets, else at the arc's end,
for 9 times up to the profile's multiplier by charge, with the school's state lengthened by the same factor. `LIVE`: a
chain of 10 nodes that keep 92% of their velocity a tick and are drawn toward the whip aim (85% of the way at the hand,
20% at the tip), held to 4 blocks a tick, to 1.2 times each link's rest length and out of blocks. The outer half's
swept segments hit what they cross (`ManipulationCombatHelper.swept`), one hit per creature per 10 ticks. Damage runs
from 3 at a tip speed of 0.35 blocks a tick to 6 at 1.0, times the spec's scale and Crimson Mastery; a stroke past a
quarter turn falls to 3 until it reverses or rests. A stroke that reverses or ends with the tip at 0.9 or faster cracks
(once per 20 ticks): every harmable body within 1.25 of the tip takes 9 and the school's state for 240 ticks.
`FADING`: after 6 ticks at rest the strand shortens to nothing over 30 ticks, for no blood; a flick revives it, and a
finished fade is the orb again.

The lash swings along a **whip aim**, not the look. On the casting client the whole of each mouse turn goes to the whip
aim and the view takes a capped share (`LashCamera`, `LashCameraRules`, `MixinMouseHandler`): at most 4 degrees a tick,
the excess dropped, coasting to rest at 60% of its rate a tick once the hand stops. The client config
`lashCameraDamping` (0 to 1) blends the cap in; at 0 the whip aim is the look. The client sends the whip aim each tick
while the lash is live or fading; the whip aim leads the view by at most 70 degrees to either side and 49 up or down, and loses 12% of that lead a tick, so it comes back to the crosshair by itself and cannot be left behind the head (`LashCameraRules.lead`); the server holds it within 85 degrees of its own copy of the look and 60 degrees a
tick (`StrandService.aim`), and relays it to watchers (`LashAimSyncPacket`). Every number above is a `LashTuning`
default; `lashTuningClient` re-reads them from `lash-tuning.json` while the game runs.

Rules that close the gaps between the two halves and between client and server: a throw tests its whole length, so it
cracks on a body at arm's length as surely as on one at the tip (live sweeps test the outer half only); a crack never
reaches a body with a block between it and the crack's point; a tap clears the body's hurt cooldown, as a crack does, so
a paid tap is never swallowed; the attack button will not let an orb go until it is half gathered
(`LashTuning.releaseMinCharge`), and the snap's cooldown is kept per player across sessions, so reopening a lash is not a
free crack; a lash's pulse is priced by the ticks since the last pulse (charge rate while gathering, the spec's rate while
thrown or live, nothing while fading; `StrandSculpting.lashPrice`), so resting just before a pulse does not make the
stroke free; the server takes at most four whip aims between two steps of the lash, moves the aim no further than one
step's limit however many arrive, and treats a step with no aim as late rather than still for three steps, so jitter
neither rests a stroke nor refreshes one; and a flick while the server's copy is still fading throws afresh with no
charge. On the client the view passes a turn under the cap whole and only coasts after a capped flick, once the mouse
has been silent for half a tick.

| Lash | Tap damage | Tap blood | Tap cooldown | Tap state | Charge blood a pulse | Full charge | Full-charge crack |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Blood Lash | 4.5 x 0.6 | 8 | 12 t | none | 7.5 | 20 t | x 1.4 |
| Searing Lash | 7 | 24 | 20 t | Searing 80 t | 30 | 40 t | x 1.75 |
| Gloam Laceration | 4.5 x 0.85, in three tails | 12 | 6 t | Obscured 60 t, on the third tap of a chain only | 20 | 30 t | x 1.25 |

**The snap** (left click while a strand is out, `StrandSnapPacket`,
guarded and paced to one per 5 ticks) forces the accent for the spec's snap blood (20 to 40 mL, through the cost
ledger, source `strand_snap`): a live or fading lash cracks at the first body down the crosshair, else at its tip, and
its whip aim comes back to the look (10-tick cooldown; on the orb the click instead lets the charge go the same way for
no snap blood), the jet spends its pressure
in one hit (3 to 9), the spray drenches (twice the damage, half again the reach), the plant erupts at once, the brand
sets at once. A snap with no strand out, or whose accent cannot act, pays nothing.

**Hits.** `StrandHits.strike` asks `canHarm`, opens the manipulation's cast scope at the last pulse's strength (a dry
strand hits at 0.75 and its accents' states run 0.75 as long), makes a new root attack, and lands it as damage only, or
for an accent with the school's state at its long duration. Its cast impact is the new **sweep** delivery (a bowed cut
along the stroke) for a lash, a shot for a jet, an area for a spray or plant. A creature the caster may not harm is
never gathered, so it neither takes a hit nor shields the one behind it. Any strand hit ends the caster's own Marionette
channel, as any cast does. Temper is burned per pulse by the Track 4 rule (0.5 a pulse); accents take no Temper of
their own.

**The brand** is the creature attachment `hemomancy:strand_brand` (`StrandBrand`: caster, school, lapse time; saved with
the creature, taken off once it lapses). **The plant's eruption** waits in `StrandService` (session state); a plant whose
caster has gone fizzles. **Blood Binding is the Animus brand** (round two P5): `BloodBindingSculpting` calls
`StrandService.brand` on every creature its pulse holds, so the bound creature carries the binder's Animus brand for as
long as the binder's Deep Brand allows, refreshed each pulse; the set flourish shows only when no brand of theirs was
already on it.

**A plant runs along a wet stain** (round two P5). When the block a plant sinks into carries a wet stain on the struck
face (`GroundNetwork.wetStainAt`), the eruption does not ring: `PlantRules.stainRun` floods the wet stain cells joined to
it through their six neighbours, no further than 8 blocks from the start in any axis, nearest first, up to
`PlantRules.stainCells` (4 plus 2 a sunk pulse, at most 20). Each cell erupts 2 ticks after the last, 0.75 wide, for the
plant's damage by blood sunk, and all the cells share one struck set, so a creature over several cells is hit once.
Each erupting cell spends the stain's wet blood: it goes tacky through `PlayerBlockEdits` (`GroundNetwork.spendStain`).
The run is fixed when the plant goes off. A plant on bare ground rings as before.

**The strand skill line** (Living Staff branch, round two P5; numbers in `StrandSkills`, read through
`SkillPointHelper`; the server reads them when a strand opens and the cue carries the one each client needs to run the
caster's motion):

| Skill | What a level does |
| --- | --- |
| Long Strand (3) | A lash's length and the pick's reach x1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3 (`StrandSculpting.reachScale(Player)`, `StrandService.length`), and the eight held manipulations' reach by the same (`HeldSkills.reach`) |
| Taut Line (2) | The lash's tip is drawn to the whip aim 20% harder a level (`LashRules.pull`'s `taut`). Its jet half (25% faster a level) is dropped from the skill and acts only on the test kit |
| Free Hand (3) | +0.1 pace a level with a lash or a held manipulation out, never past walking |
| Whipcrack (3) | A lash's crack and a held manipulation's attack-button hit land 15% harder and lay their state 20% longer a level |
| Deep Brand (2) | A Blood Binding's brand lasts 900 then 1200 ticks (45, 60 seconds; 30 untrained). Its set-speed half is dropped from the skill |
| Second Strand (1, Degree 6) | The twin (CL-27), below |

**Second Strand: the twin** (CL-27; the lash twin only, CQ-22 A). Vanilla uses one item at a time, so the off hand's strand is a twin of the open one,
not a second channel. It pours when Second Strand is unlocked and the hand opposite the channelling hand is empty or
holds a cell hand, decided when the strand opens. Every pulse costs half again (`VerbSculpting.bloodPerPulse(Player)`,
read by the price, the HUD and the tests). A twin lash is a second chain from the off hand, a little slacker (0.85 of the
lead's tautness), whose sweeps hit for half with their own lockouts and never crack. A twin jet hits 1.4 times as hard. A
twin spray's cone opens from 35 to 50 degrees. A twin plant sinks two pulses for one paid. A twin brand, when it sets,
also brands the nearest other harmable creature within 4 blocks. Clients draw the twin from the off hand, and its arm
points along it in third person and works it in first person when the off hand holds a cell hand.

**Absorption's half (CL-24, CL-26).** The draw's damage is `hemomancy:blood_absorption` (tags `bypasses_armor` and
`no_knockback`): it names the drawer, so the creature turns on them and its death is credited; `HemoDamageTypes.paysKillBounty`
keeps kill blood and the Temperament kill shift off a kill by draw. The draw is scaled by Crimson Mastery and by the
rider table `AbsorptionRiders` (common/damage, pure) keyed by the school state the creature carries; several states
give every rider at once. `AbsorptionRiderEffects` applies them after each pulse:

| State | Rider |
| --- | --- |
| Pressure | Pulled toward the drawer; 1.25 times the blood back |
| Searing | 1.5 times the draw; 0.6 times the blood back |
| Rime | Slowness II for 15 ticks; held still at Rime 3 |
| Lodestone | Armour halved while the draw holds (15 ticks) |
| Necrosis | A kill by draw spreads Necrosis within 3 blocks |
| Disrupted | Half the draw arcs to the nearest other marked creature within 6 |
| Illuminated | Drawn from 1.5 times the reach |
| Obscured | Loses its target; the drawer is Veiled for 60 ticks |

The bare hand and the Staff take the drawer's branded creatures first (`BloodAbsorptionTargetRules.orderTargets`), from
twice the reach. **Client.** Each client runs the same rule class from the caster's look (`StrandClientState`, the
caster's own exact look, another player's synced look) and draws its own copy (`StrandRenderer`, from the school's flow
materials, Searing Lash with the flame sheath and molten core); the server sends one keyed `STRAND` cue when a strand
opens and refreshes it each pulse, and `STRAND_ACCENT` bursts for cracks, pierces, drenches, eruptions, brands and the
plant's telegraph. The holding arm points along the strand in third person (`PlayerAnimationRegistry` entry
`strand_stroke`), the hand pours no ordinary stream while a strand is out, and the verb HUD shows a jet's pressure, a
plant's sunk blood or a brand's hold as a thin arc round the crosshair. **First person** (round two P5,
`CellHandItemRenderer.applyStrandArmTransform`): instead of the idle wave, a lash's arm leads the stroke toward the
chain's second node with a throw through after a reversal, a jet's arm is thrust out and braced with a tremor that grows
with pressure, a spray's open palm rolls side to side, a plant's palm pitches down as it fills, and a brand's arm draws
slowly back as it takes. The second wave draws in its school (`StrandSchoolGeometry`): a dark lash edged in pale light
for Tenebris, cruor shards riding a Congeatio jet into a spearhead, blood-iron flechettes streaming down a Ferric jet and
across a Ferric spray and iron spikes driven up by a Ferric eruption (all in the solid pass), jagged re-forking arcs for
a Ductilis spray or brand, prism rays for a Lux spray, and a fire column at a Flammeus eruption. An eruption throws about
three spikes per small stain cell and up to twelve for a full ring.

### 8.1 Manipulation Properties

Each manipulation has:
- **Name** — registry ID
- **Blood cost** — drained from the player's blood volume (modified by Efficiency skill, purity penalty, and Blood Drunkenness)
- **XP cost** — additional experience cost
- **Alignment level** — required temper alignment
- **Type** — `QUICK`, `CHARGED`, `PASSIVE`, or `CONTINUOUS`
- **Rank** — `HUMILIS`, `MEDIOCRITAS`, `SUMMA`, `MAGISTER`, `PERFECTUS`
- **Temper** — the primary blood temper used for unlocks, tree placement, rendering color, and organization
- **Secondary temper** — optional mixed affinity used for temper gain, detail-panel display, and combat damage composition
- **Vein Section** — which vein section takes strain when cast
- **Cooldown** — tick-based cooldown between uses
- **ManipLevel** — manipulations level up with use

Shared degree gates for manipulation ranks are centralized in `ManipulationRankGates` and used by full Blood Memory items, crude memory shards, and the manipulation progress UI:

| Rank | Required Initiatory Degree |
|------|----------------------------|
| `HUMILIS` | 0 |
| `MEDIOCRITAS` | 1 |
| `SUMMA` | 3 |
| `MAGISTER` | 5 |
| `PERFECTUS` | 6 |

Secondary tempers do not change a manipulation's required alignment, tree cluster, primary color, Dynamic Use match, or Sporitic Thurible cost/cooldown affinity. On cast, the primary temper gains the configured manipulation-use amount and the secondary temper, when present, gains half that amount. For direct manipulation damage and Living Staff weapon-form combat, mixed-temper damage is composition-based rather than additive: pure manipulations use the full primary affinity multiplier, while mixed manipulations use the better of the full primary multiplier or the 75% primary / 25% secondary blend (`TemperAffinityRules`). A secondary temper can lift a matchup but never weakens it.

Manipulation types are input contracts: **Quick** fires once on key press; **Charged** gains strength while held, fires each time it fills, and normally fires its partial charge on release with proportional blood cost; **Passive** toggles criteria-driven effects on or off; **Continuous** starts on press, pays its registered blood cost for an immediate pulse and each subsequent one-second pulse, and starts its cooldown when released or interrupted. Ironhearted is the deliberate charged exception: releasing before 40 ticks fails before blood, effect, mastery, or cooldown and leaves no partial Iron Heart.

Charged casts since balance pass 2 (`ManipulationCastingRules`, `ManipulationChargeClock`):

- **Charge floor.** A release below 50% charge fizzles before payment with "Not enough charge" (CB-6, ruled 2026-11-13; it was 25%). Quick, Continuous and Passive manipulations ignore the floor; spells that already require a full charge (Hematic Mortar, Blood Needle Lance, Ironhearted, Thread Ripper) are unchanged.
- **Rewards follow the charge.** Alignment gain and skill-point payout scale with the released charge fraction, and a cast below half charge earns no manipulation-mastery use and does not count toward the manipulation-use milestones.
- **Server-observed charge.** The charge clock starts when the server receives the first charge update (`CastingChargePacket`, held 1) for the selected manipulation. The server credits at most the hold it observed since then plus a tolerance of max(2 ticks, 15% of the observed hold), so ordinary tick-rate jitter does not strip a full charge. A key-down older than twice the required charge plus 20 ticks is stale and counts as none, so a key-down left behind by a refused cast cannot credit a much later release. A release with no live key-down is ignored silently; holding through a long cooldown therefore needs a fresh press.

### 8.2 Registered Manipulations

`ManipulationInit` registers 115 blood manipulations (2026-11-10): the 108 that stood before the core loop, plus the Tendon Line, Blood Lash, Lode Draw, Hematic Hewing, Conjure Pickaxe, Living Land and Venous Cling that it added; no retired compatibility ids remain (`ManipulationCastFixGameTests.registryTypesMatchUnifiedInputSemantics` pins 115 and 75 QUICK). The catalog below tracks every entry and its developer-facing gameplay role. The Temper column lists the primary temper, then the secondary where one is assigned; the Tempers tab detail panel shows both.

Twelve active families containing 29 deeper forms (`ManipulationFamilyRegistry`) share one `ManipLevel`: learning a form preserves the family's highest level and XP, while a deeper form requires the stated family-mastery stage. Forms are distinct registered manipulations and Blood Memory items, not replacements for the baseline form.

**Damage prices by rank (LP-12, NQ-04-6, built 2026-11-15).** A damaging R cast buys at least 0.020, 0.025, 0.031, 0.039 or 0.049 HP per mL at Humilis, Mediocritas, Summa, Magister and Perfectus. Damage is read at full charge with no conditional bonus: a bolt on one body, an area cast on three. Prices were only cut, rounded to 5 mL, and casts already at or above the target kept theirs; the updrafts are priced for movement and stay out. Twelve casts moved: Insatiable Hunger 225 to 100, Cruor Javelin 200 to 160, Searing Lash 225 to 160, Blood Aneurysm 400 to 260, Bloom of Rot 500 to 290, Fruiting Contagion 400 to 290, Sanguine Magnetism 450 to 385, Rimebound Sentence 750 to 310, White Verdict 800 to 735, Funeral Bell 1000 to 430, Lodestone Collapse 900 to 610, Synaptic Storm 900 to 490. The sheet is [04-T5c-price-sheet.csv](owner_answers/04-T5c-price-sheet.csv).
