## 16. Morphlings

A Morphling is a cultivated fungal strain worn on the body. The host feeds it blood; it reshapes the host and lends it powers in return. Each strain has convergently grown an animal's body solution (a sailfish's sail, a sea lily's stalk, a hydra's budding) without being that animal, and each lives with a partner organism, an alga, bacterium or yeast suited to its water, that decides what it can do. The eight strains are the hereditary strains of the Brined Court's eight houses, shallow to deep. The Order meets them first as specimens and catalogues them without house names; a strain's house line appears only once the player knows of the Court (decision M7, "Strain text" below). Per-stage numbers are in [`docs/MORPHLING_STRAINS.md`](MORPHLING_STRAINS.md); the design is `docs/archive/tracks/brined_court/design/BRINED_COURT_HOUSES_WORKING_DESIGN.md`, "Strain powers and appearance".

### 16.1 Types

The eight strains replaced the first-attempt strains (Lumenlace, Irontooth, Deadman's Purse, Witch's Ear, Bootlace, Winter Shroud, Gravecap, Emberfang), which were deleted outright with no migration (Brined Court Track 1, 2026-10-29). Every per-strain fact lives in one row of `MorphlingStrains` (`common/item/harbinger/morphlings/`): item and passive effect (`morphling_<id>`), tempers, house, home condition, Cradle flag, Last Rite, wild polyp family, HUD sprite and accent, and creative order. Code reads the row; `MorphlingStrainTableGuardrailTest` rejects a hard-coded `morphling_<strain>` id outside the table and `ItemInit`, and any trace of the old names under `src/`. Each strain item is a `HouseMorphlingItem` subclass (`SunburstMorphlingItem`, ...).

| Strain | Classification | Preferred / Secondary | House | Cradle at Primal | Last Rite | Polyp family | Incubation catalysts (plus Rotten Flesh) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ![](../src/main/resources/assets/hemomancy/textures/item/morphling_sunburst.png) Sunburst | *Heliophyta donans* | Lux / Ferric | The Giving Light | yes | — | sun alga | Hematic Algal Crust, Sea Pickle |
| ![](../src/main/resources/assets/hemomancy/textures/item/morphling_holdfast.png) Holdfast | *Hapterophyta tenax* | Ferric / Animus | The Holding Stone | yes | — | coralline alga | Chitinous Husk, Kelp |
| ![](../src/main/resources/assets/hemomancy/textures/item/morphling_mermaids_purse.png) Mermaid's Purse | *Sanguibursa communis* | Animus / Ductilis | The Shared Wake | yes | — | gut bacteria | Raw Pelagic Herring, Cod |
| ![](../src/main/resources/assets/hemomancy/textures/item/morphling_dead_mans_rope.png) Dead Man's Rope | *Funiculospora nexilis* | Ductilis / Tenebris | The Woven Current | no | — | light bacteria | Ganglion Cluster, Glow Ink Sac |
| ![](../src/main/resources/assets/hemomancy/textures/item/morphling_ink_cap.png) Ink Cap | *Atramentaria velata* | Tenebris / Ductilis | The Veiled Fold | no | `hemomancy:ink_mantle` at Apex | black yeast | Ink Sac, Chromatophores |
| ![](../src/main/resources/assets/hemomancy/textures/item/morphling_hushbell.png) Hushbell | *Campanospora silens* | Congeatio / Tenebris | The Still Bell | yes | `hemomancy:cryptobiosis` at Primal | cold bacteria | Cleansing Hemolymph, Packed Ice |
| ![](../src/main/resources/assets/hemomancy/textures/item/morphling_marrowplume.png) Marrowplume | *Medullophyta ossivora* | Mortem / Congeatio | Last Marrow | yes | — | bone bacteria | Bone Worm Colony, Bone |
| ![](../src/main/resources/assets/hemomancy/textures/item/morphling_kinbud.png) Kinbud | *Pyrrhiza gemmans* | Flammeus / Mortem | The Kindling | no | — | vent bacteria | Giant Tube Worm Colony, Magma Cream |

Secondary tempers follow the depth gradient: each strain leans toward its inward neighbour. The Latin is the Order's pseudo-classification: raised strains take plant-, spore- or root-style genera (*-phyta*, *-spora*, *-rhiza*, *-bursa*, *-aria*), which keeps them apart from refined fungal scars (*-myces*). Mermaid's Purse keeps Deadman's Purse's genus and Kinbud keeps Emberfang's, as traces.

#### Ladders and home conditions

Built in Brined Court Track 2. The passive works from Unfed and scales with every stage; Developing, Mature and Apex each add one reactive power (Apex's is the signature, with the longest cooldown); Primal is the Morphic Nectar capstone (§16.3.1). A strain's **home** is its house's habitat, felt anywhere in the world: unless a power says otherwise it gives +50% to durations and rates and +25% to radii, and a few powers work only at home.

| Strain | Home | Passive | Developing | Mature | Apex | Primal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sunburst | daylight under open sky, or sunlit water | Sun-Fed (home only: no upkeep, hunger then blood) | Shared Table | Lantern Fronds | Bloom (home only) | Arbor |
| Holdfast | on or against stone, or submerged | Grip | Cling | Brace | Breakwater | The Holding |
| Mermaid's Purse | sprint-swimming, open ocean, or an ally within 8 | Purse Siphon | Feed Banking | School's Share | Raise the Sail | Shared Wake |
| Dead Man's Rope | submerged, or holding a strand | Lateral Strands | Lifeline | Strand Link | Colony | Red Rope |
| Ink Cap | light 7 or lower, or submerged | Veil | Ink Wake | Folded Away (home only) | Ink Reprieve (death-save) | Deliquesce |
| Hushbell | cold biome, deep water, or standing still | Hush | Cryptobiotic Hide | Cold Cleanse | Fold Shut | Cryptobiosis (death-save) |
| Marrowplume | bone blocks within 8, or a kill in the last 30 s | Marrow Feeding | Plume Cloud | Root Network | Fall's Inheritance | Whale Fall |
| Kinbud | near heat (lava, magma, fire, hot biomes, the Nether, vents) | Cultivated Mending | Nematocyst Sting | Grasping Crown | Second Head | Kindled |

- **Death-saves.** Two, both in the shared Last Rite group (10-minute cooldown): Ink Cap's Ink Reprieve at Apex (500 mL, `hemomancy:ink_mantle`) and Hushbell's Cryptobiosis at Primal (650 mL, `hemomancy:cryptobiosis`). Lumenlace's Last-Light Mantle (`hemomancy:last_light`) is retired. Sunburst has no self death-save; its rescue always goes to others.
- **Balance rules.** Repeatable Primals cost 250-450 mL on 12-90 s cooldowns; reactive cooldowns sit in bands (Developing 3-15 s, Mature 8-20 s, Apex 20-60 s); every power below Primal does something for a host alone; health moved to protect others never takes the giver below a floor (50% Shared Table and Colony, 30% Breakwater); all Morphling healing of the host claims the circulation window; bonus loot excludes players, bosses and spawner mobs. `MorphlingBalanceBandsTest` checks the ladders.
- **Boundaries.** No strain grants thorns, retaliation, toughness or plating (the armour sets own those). Kinbud's Second Head is part of the host's body, not a summon: it isn't commanded and doesn't count toward Puppet Interference. Anchoring (Holdfast, Sunburst's Arbor, Marrowplume in a Whale Fall) is a reversible hold, never petrification.
- **Shared effects.** Stung (Kinbud; 1 damage a second, its own damage type, affects undead, not Poison), Pinned and Sealed (the one Morphling lock, folded into `Paralysis.blocksActions` and the paralysis movement checks).

#### Strain text

Brined Court Track 4. All strain text is lang keys. A strain item's tooltip reads, under its name: the greyed binomial (`morphling.hemomancy.<id>.binomial`), the Order's one-line description (`.description`), the organism's look at the current stage (`.stage.<unfed|fledgling|developing|mature|apex|primal>`), then tempers, maturity and bonding, and the maturity bonus list (`message.hemomancy.<id>_morphling_item.passive` from Unfed, then the four ladder powers). Each partner family's Living Bestiary entry (`bestiary.hemomancy.morphling.<family>.title/description/source`) is a field note in the Alchemist's voice: the fungus, the form it converges on and its partner, phrased as observations. The Alchemist answers an item inquiry for each strain (`dialogue_inquiry/alchemist/hemomancy/morphling_<id>.json`). The Liber Sanguinium's Hematic Order chapter has three Morphling pages: cultivation, the eight strains, and the Cradle and Morphic Nectar.

None of that text names a house or the Court. Once the player knows of the Court, the tooltip adds a house line (`morphling.hemomancy.<id>.court`: "Raised by the Giving Light. Its partner is ...") and the Bestiary entry a Court paragraph (`bestiary.hemomancy.morphling.<family>.court`). Both read `CourtKnowledge.isKnown(player)` (`common/capability/player/harbinger/court/`), which reads the owner's synced `CourtProgress` (Track 5, §29 "Learning of the Court"). `MorphlingStrainTextResourceTest` checks that every strain has all of these keys, that the Order's text names no house, that the Liber lists match the table, and that the strain text uses no God or devil framing and no "many-headed" for Dead Man's Rope.

### 16.2 Cultivation

- Start with a **Morphling Polyp** ![Morphling Polyp](../src/main/resources/assets/hemomancy/textures/item/morphling_polyp.png) (base form)
- Players can obtain their first Morphling Polyp from rare layered wild polyps: black slime-like morphling larvae that spawn across the Overworld carrying up to three partner families picked up from where they grew, each hinting at a strain they can become.
- Wild Morphling Polyps sink through water and settle on the seabed, drifting or pursuing targets horizontally instead of swimming upward. They can survive underwater and retain their hopping movement on land.
- Degree 2+ players can also capture wild Morphling Polyps in **Specimen Jars** and bring them to the Alchemist's Living Bestiary. Recording a captured polyp logs its layer families; surrendering it converts one stored layer into a matching wild-bound morphling item.
- The eight layer families (`MorphlingPolypLayer`) are named for each strain's partner organism: sun alga (Sunburst), coralline alga (Holdfast), gut bacteria (Mermaid's Purse), light bacteria (Dead Man's Rope), black yeast (Ink Cap), cold bacteria (Hushbell), bone bacteria (Marrowplume) and vent bacteria (Kinbud). A family's hint item is its strain's incubation catalyst.
- Wild-bound morphlings are immediately equipable and start at Developing maturity, but their stack carries `WildBound` and cannot mature past Developing. They must first absorb the Developing-stage blood quota while equipped; their next successful **Morphling Incubator** cycle clears `WildBound` and advances them to Mature.
- Incubate in a **Morphling Incubator** (Degree 5) with enzymes; each feeding raises the strain one stage. The preferred enzyme counts in full, the secondary at 75%, any other at 50%.
- Store morphlings in a **Morphling Jar** ![Morphling Jar](../src/main/resources/assets/hemomancy/textures/item/morphling_jar.png) (6 slots, Uncommon rarity). The jar now opens one unified container screen: the six real inventory slots sit in two side columns around the animated bouncing morphling display, and clicking a swimming morphling equips or unequips it without leaving the inventory view.
- The **Living Staff** cycles through equipped morphlings and changes its topper model accordingly

### 16.3 Maturity System

**Current implementation note:** Morphlings have six code-facing states: the `Unfed` baseline plus five earned maturity levels, `Fledgling -> Developing -> Mature -> Apex -> Primal`. Every Incubator feeding advances at most one stage. Unfed can enter its first incubation immediately; Fledgling, Developing, and Mature Morphlings must respectively absorb 50, 100, and 200 blood through successful equipped upkeep before the next incubation. Excess enzyme inputs remain in the Incubator. Blood progress resets on advancement and cannot be banked across stages. If passive Morphling upkeep is disabled, the blood-bond gate is bypassed to prevent a progression lock. **Primal** remains a nectar-only capstone backed by `Primalized`.

Each morphling has a **maturity level** (0–5) that determines its power and which reactive abilities it has:

| Maturity | Name | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| 0 | Unfed | Baseline state before successful feeding |
| 1 | Fledgling | Passive only, stronger than at Unfed |
| 2 | Developing | First reactive power |
| 3 | Mature | Second reactive power |
| 4 | Apex | Signature power, with the longest reactive cooldown (Ink Cap's is its death-save) |
| 5 | Primal | Nectar-transformed Apex form. Unlocks a late-game active or loop-defining capstone power. |

Each morphling type has a **preferred temper** and **secondary temper**. These affinities determine effective enzyme power; the Incubator consumes the smallest sufficient subset for the next single stage and leaves unneeded inputs in place. The passive effect's amplifier scales with maturity level.

### 16.3.1 Primal Morphlings

Primal morphlings are the true fourth player-facing capstone above Apex. To primalize a morphling, throw an **Apex** morphling item into a pool of **Morphic Nectar** while a nearby/throwing `ServerPlayer` has completed **Apotheos** (`getArchonPath() == EnumArchonPath.APOTHEOS`; a Degree 8 Silentium is refused). The special Primal transform path runs before normal Morphic Nectar recipes. It refuses non-Apex morphlings, already-Primal morphlings, and players below Apotheos degree 8.

The transform preserves the item stack's morphling identity, existing custom data, feedings/enzyme power, cooldowns, and nectar mutation marker. Primal powers intentionally fill late-game gameplay roles rather than acting as simple numeric upgrades. Existing Apex powers still count Primal morphlings as Apex-or-better for compatibility.

Successful Primal powers apply **Morphic Strain** as the main fungal drawback alongside blood cost and cooldown. Morphic Strain is lighter than Hematic Strain: it modestly reduces max health and movement speed, uses fungal visual feedback, and is capped before it becomes a hard lockout.

Per-strain Primals (Brined Court Track 2): Sunburst Arbor, Holdfast The Holding, Mermaid's Purse Shared Wake, Dead Man's Rope Red Rope, Ink Cap Deliquesce and Kinbud Kindled are paid actives (250-450 mL, 12-90 s) used through the Living Staff, each with its own blood source; Marrowplume's Whale Fall triggers on a kill of 20+ maximum health and costs nothing; Hushbell's Cryptobiosis is the Last Rite death-save. Numbers in `docs/MORPHLING_STRAINS.md`.

### 16.3.2 Morphic Nectar Mutation Display

Any item transformed through Morphic Nectar receives the `MorphicNectarMutated` stack marker via `MorphicNectarMutationRules.markMutated`. Mutated items gain a tooltip line (`Morphic Nectar-mutated`) and a client-side inventory decorator. Generic nectar-mutated items use a dark organic green frame. Primal morphlings use a stronger red/green/yellow animated tendril overlay rendered procedurally over the item slot.

The Primal decorator is intentionally not a static frame: it uses a small set of animated, high-resolution procedural tendrils drawn with the GUI render type so the item reads as actively writhing while staying legible at inventory scale. The current tuning uses 5 tendrils, 42 curve samples, 3 layered passes, a 1.25 px body width, and trimmed endpoints to avoid a filled-in slot mask.

### 16.4 Morphling Cradle

The **Morphling Cradle** (`MorphlingCradleBlockEntity`; raised by the Degree 4 lesser Working craft `working/morphling_cradle` since 2026-11-03) is an owner-bound support station for hosting a single morphling item outside the staff.

- Supports **floor / wall / ceiling** placement (`AttachFace` + `FACING` state)
- Only the bound owner can swap/remove the hosted morphling
- Applies hosted morphling support effects to the owner and valid bloodline members in range
- Uses staged upkeep/action blood costs, with fallback draw from owner bloodline pool when enabled
- Can leech nearby valid hostile targets into a cradle blood buffer and redistribute that blood to nearby cradles / owner blood volume
- Recognizes Primal maturity (`level 5`) but only the support strains flagged `cradlePrimal` in `MorphlingStrains` can be hosted while Primal: Sunburst, Holdfast, Mermaid's Purse, Hushbell and Marrowplume.

### 16.5 Client Mutation Rendering

An equipped Morphling changes the player stage by stage, as the Brined Court spec's appearance tables describe (Track 3, `docs/archive/tracks/brined_court/03-strain-visuals.md`).

- `MorphlingMutationRegistry` builds one `MorphlingVisualMutation` per strain from the table row: the row's `tintColor` (the Unfed–Fledgling look; alpha is the overlay opacity at Apex), how that tint moves (Sunburst a slow warm emissive pulse, Mermaid's Purse a lateral-line shimmer, Dead Man's Rope a fast emissive streaming pulse, Hushbell a held breath, Kinbud an amber flicker over pale skin), and one `MorphlingStrainAttachment` per anchor.
- A mutation holds **several** attachments (`attachments`); `MorphlingMutationLayer` draws the tint, then each attachment, and `MorphlingPlayerPartVisibility` hides the union of the parts they replace.
- The attachment models are generated by `tools/model_export/morphling_strains.py` (one function per strain): a Java model per anchor under `client/model/entity/morphling/` (`SunburstBodyModel`, `HoldfastArmModel`, …), its atlas and glow atlas under `textures/models/morphling/<strain>_<anchor>.png`, a Blockbench project under `models/entity/bbmodel/morphling/` and a stage-by-stage preview under `build/morphling-strain-preview/`. Textures are one pixel per model unit (16 px per block, the skin's own density). `MorphlingStrainModels` (generated) lists every anchor; `LayerEvents` registers them all from it.
- Every generated part carries the stage it grows at, a limb tag (`UPPER`/`LOWER` on arm and leg parts, for the Court NPCs' jointed rig, which draws them per segment with `MorphlingStrainModel.drawLimbSegment`), a motion and the `MorphlingActiveState` bits it answers. A part grows in over its first stages (0.7, 0.88, then full size), so a strain reads as one organism growing. `Unfed`/`Fledgling` are tint only.
- Motion comes from animation time and the synced active bits, settling rather than snapping (`MorphlingAnimContext`, curves in `MorphlingStrainMotion`): Sunburst's fronds open with daylight and fully during Lantern Fronds, Bloom and Arbor; Holdfast's grip strands splay and its anchor strands grow into the ground while anchored; Mermaid's Purse's sail lies flat and raises and flushes with Raise the Sail, and its flank purses swell with banked blood (the fill sixteenths); Dead Man's Rope's veins carry a pulse group by group and its ribbons drift; Ink Cap's rim drips; Hushbell's mantle breathes, then holds still, and at Primal its bell closes over the head (hiding it) during Fold Shut and Cryptobiosis; Marrowplume's plumes sway and beads drip; Kinbud's mane ripples like flame (stronger while Kindled) and its Second Heads bud on their own necks from the right shoulder (`SECOND_HEAD`) and the left (`SECOND_HEAD_TWIN`).

| Strain | Anchors (first stage) |
| --- | --- |
| Sunburst | BODY (Developing) |
| Holdfast | ARMS (Developing), LEGS (Apex); 1.12x at Primal |
| Mermaid's Purse | BODY, ARMS, LEGS (Developing), HEAD brow crest (Primal) |
| Dead Man's Rope | ARMS (Developing), BODY (Mature) |
| Ink Cap | HEAD (Developing; replaces the head at Primal), BODY veil (Primal) |
| Hushbell | BODY (Developing) |
| Marrowplume | ARMS (Developing), LEGS (Apex) |
| Kinbud | BODY spine (Developing), HEAD nape and crown (Developing; replaces the head at Primal) |

Helmets: below Primal a worn helmet wins and head growths are not drawn; at Primal a head replacement (Ink Cap's hood, Kinbud's polyp face) takes the head and the helmet still renders over it. `MixinHumanoidArmorLayer` applies the hidden set to armour; `MixinPlayerItemInHandLayer` hides held items for hidden arms. `render_layers.renderMorphlingMutationLayer=false` disables the tint and every attachment.

World-space pieces are drawn by `MorphlingStrainWorldRenderer` from `WorldEffectDispatcher` on the shared toolkit (`OutpouringBrushes`: the Lux, Umbra, Mortem and Glass materials), never vanilla particles: Dead Man's Rope strands to linked entities, block anchors and the Lifeline point (where the host stood when the bit came on), with beads and a pulse running along each; its Primal train laid along where the host walked; the Bloom (a floating gold mat with turning fronds) and Whale Fall (a pale stain beaded red with swaying plumes) field patches; Holdfast's grip strands, Sunburst's Arbor roots and Marrowplume's Whale Fall stalks spreading from the feet; Ink Cap's Deliquesce dissolve; Hushbell's frost seal; Mermaid's Purse's wake with the sail up. `MorphlingStrainClientEvents` keeps the trail memory (`MorphlingStrainTrails`) and sheds sparse accents (ink motes, blood beads, frost, Kindled sparks).

The HUD sprites (`textures/gui/morphling_overlay/`, 32x32 static plus `anim/` and `anim2/` strips) are exported from the item icons' pixel maps by `docs/archive/concept/output/brined-strain-icons-16x16/export_hud_sprites.py`, which writes `hud-pixel-maps.json` and adds the feeding tendril that hooks the vessel at the HUD's feeding point.

`morphlingStrainReviewClient` captures every strain at all six stages from the back, side and front, every active state, underwater and night variants and a helmeted Primal player into `build/morphling-strain-review/screenshots`; `tools/review/morphling_strain_contact.py` builds the Apex contact sheet and per-strain stage sheets from them.

The Mycophant Tendril's full-body fungalization still uses the first-attempt fungal head, kept under a neutral name as `FungalHeadAttachmentModel` (`client/model/entity/morphling/`, texture `textures/models/morphling/fungal_head.png`). Its Blockbench project regenerates with `node tools/model_export/java_model_to_bbmodel.mjs --set=morphling`.

Multiplayer sync relies on the equipped-morphling capability and `SyncEquippedMorphlingPacket` (the stack, the active bits and the strands), sent to the owner and trackers by `EquippedMorphlingEvents`.

### 16.6 Puppet Interference

An equipped Morphling detects any valid active same-owner shaped puppet or Commandeered Will in the owner's dimension. While at least one qualifies, final Morphling blood upkeep is multiplied by **1.25** through the existing Blood Flow Ledger. The multiplier is boolean rather than per-puppet, ends as soon as the last qualifying tether disappears, and does not increase bonding blood, maturity, husbandry, borrowed blood, or Thelemic reserve progress. Trial summons, foreign or unowned bodies, dead or unloaded bodies, stale owner sessions, and cross-dimension bodies do not qualify. The HUD reports `Distracted — 125% blood upkeep` while active. The puppets pay too: 75% tether range and x1.5 thread upkeep (§17 "Morphling interference").

## 17. Puppeteering & Summons

The puppeteer summon system is a Harbinger-side control-tool path rather than another blood manipulation category.

- **Progression role:** Degree 2 only foreshadows the art through Blood Drunk Puppeteer encounters and Enthralling Filament. Practical puppeteering starts at Degree 3, after the Mnemonist's memory-preparation lesson, so the system reads as memory externalized into a controlled body. Degree 4 deepens the path with heavier summons, and Degree 5 introduces the memory-replay specialist.
- **Control tool:** `marionette_crossbar` / **Marionette Crossbar**. It stores a stable crossbar UUID, permanent owner attunement, prepared summon name, charge, skill-scaled capacity, persistent command mode, and an optional Guard anchor. A fresh Crossbar permanently attunes to the first player who right-clicks with it; that first use only performs attunement. Base capacity is 256; Bound Command adds 32 per level. Subsequent tap air-use calls or recalls the prepared shape. Hold air-use for 10 ticks (0.5 seconds) to open a text-only command radial: its inner ring selects **Follow**, **Guard**, **Hunt**, and **Passive** for every shaped body or Commandeered Will on that exact Crossbar. Follow stays with the puppeteer and attacks hostiles within 12 blocks; Hunt searches the full tether range. Attacking a hostile with the Crossbar in the main hand temporarily focuses those bodies regardless of their persistent mode; focus accepts Minecraft's full hostile `Enemy` category, never players or friendly bound bodies, and drops outside tether range. The item bar is always visible and displays charge rather than durability.

Held appearance (client visuals only): the Crossbar renders as a 3D bone-and-hematic-iron marionette control with five living-vein strings (head, two hand strings and two foot strings). With no puppet out it hangs still. While this Crossbar's bodies are out (matched by synced owner and Crossbar id), the bar bobs and rolls, walks its foot bar against its hand bar, and its veins pulse. Melee swings, Cinder Bellows breaths and Marrow Juggler knives tug it, and calls or recalls lift it and snap it down.

In third person, each body's control thread leaves a fixed string knot on the drawn bar, assigned in entity-id order. First person keeps the hand-estimate anchor. Vesper's held Crossbar uses the same model, and his puppets match on owner alone. Rebuild the model, atlas and BBModel with `tools/circus/build_marionette_crossbar.py`; `tools/circus/preview_marionette_crossbar.py` renders the poses.
- **Field transposition:** Shape preparation remains a Spindle-only action until the one-rank Degree 5 skill **Skein Transposition**, a sibling of Thread Economy requiring Far Tether. Once learned, the radial gains an outer ring listing every summon definition: the seven ordinary artificial shapes and the Ringmaster Pattern (`CrossbarRadialScreen` iterates `PuppeteerSummonDefinitions.all()`; whether the Pattern belongs there is audit P-12, D-38). Selecting another learned, affordable, capacity-valid shape atomically creates one replacement, spends its ordinary adjusted call charge, recalls only bodies on that exact Crossbar matching the formerly prepared shape, and commits the replacement shape. Bodies of other shapes and Commandeered Wills remain. Any failed validation or entity insertion preserves charge, preparation, and every old body. Sneak-use does not cycle shapes.
- **Field winding:** The one-rank Degree 5 skill **Sanguine Spinning**, requiring Far Tether, can be toggled from the Puppeteering tree. While enabled, an owner-attuned Crossbar held in the main hand, or otherwise the offhand, gains 1 thread charge every 20 ticks at a cost of exactly 10 blood. Full, unattuned, foreign, and inventory-only Crossbars are ignored. This automatic tool spending respects Sanguine Reserve's 15% floor and creates no physical Enthralling Filament.
- **Station:** `puppeteers_spindle` / **Puppeteer's Spindle**. It is a persistent block entity with two menu slots: a crossbar slot and a thread feeder slot. Conversion is **1 item = 8 thread charge**, and the persistent internal buffer holds 512 charge. A slotted Crossbar automatically draws from that buffer up to its owner-scaled capacity. Clicking a learned puppet row immediately prepares that shape on the Crossbar; there are no separate Attune or Prepare buttons. The Spindle also defensively attunes a fresh slotted Crossbar to the interacting player, but never overwrites a foreign owner and never calls a summon. The player removes the prepared Crossbar and performs the call in the field.
- **Spindle rendering/UI:** The placed spindle stores horizontal facing, faces the placing player, and renders through `PuppeteersSpindleRenderer` / `PuppeteersSpindleModel` with a custom item renderer instead of appearing as a venous stone brick cube. The model is a Saxony spinning wheel grown from the body: cured-wood bench on femur legs, a striated-muscle wheel on finger-bone spokes around a beating heart hub, clawed bone flyer and bobbin of sanguine thread, a fibre-dressed vertebral distaff, and a treadle/footman/crank linkage solved each frame; thread and heart veins carry an emissive layer. Geometry, atlas (`textures/entity/model_puppeteers_spindle.png` + `_glow`), Blockbench project and `PuppeteersSpindleMesh` are generated by `tools/model_export/puppeteers_spindle.py` (`--preview` writes turnaround renders to `build/`). Its screen uses a vein-pattern background, styled slot frames, crossbar/thread meters, a directly clickable summon list, and themed tooltips.
- **Unlock economy:** Seven Puppetry Cardinal Ordeals share the reusable Dominion Lesser floor. An owner-attuned Crossbar is seated as a preserved Cardinal Focus medium, a Living Staff starts the ceremony, and puppet-specific brazier offerings distinguish the ordeals. Blood and offerings commit only after successful manifestation; later failure grants nothing and does not refund them, while the Crossbar remains untouched.
- **Artificial-body lifecycle:** The Gorebound Hulk and Mnemonist Puppet reuse Zombie navigation and animation only. They are constructed puppet bodies rather than undead: neither burns in daylight, becomes a Drowned, spawns as a baby, picks up loot, nor rolls or retains ordinary Zombie equipment. Both use ground melee pursuit once the shared Crossbar controller assigns a target. The Mnemonist's stored-damage replay also operates while it is an unbound trial form, rather than being restricted to the bound version.
- **Charge economy and tether:** Summoning spends the definition's call charge; each active body independently requests its upkeep from the matching equipped Crossbar on a persistent one-minute deadline. Each bound summon renders a red tether back to its owner. If the matching Crossbar is not equipped in either hand, the summon and tether flicker/fade for a base 100 ticks (5 seconds), extended one second per Bound Command level. Re-equipping stabilizes it; failing to do so unravels that body. Insufficient upkeep unravels only the starved summon. Crossing dimensions, dying/respawning, or ending the owner session deliberately severs all affected bodies rather than preserving or teleporting them between worlds; a session token also severs bodies that were unloaded when the boundary occurred. Owner-bound bodies are persistence-required and exempt from Peaceful's automatic hostile removal, so vanilla despawn cannot bypass upkeep or recall; unbound trial forms retain hostile trial semantics.
- **Arrival and departure (`PuppetStrings`):** puppets never pop in or out. A Crossbar call or swap, a Cardinal trial manifestation and a Circus stage body each arrive with `PUPPET_DESCEND`: vein strings drop from above, the body is lowered in over 14 ticks while sinew knits up it, then the strings fray away. Departures unspool instead of discarding the body:
  - **Which exits:** recall, swap, the end of the missing-Crossbar countdown, every unravel cause (dimension, session, cap, starvation), an absent or mismatched owner, a missing Crossbar id, trial puppets cleared with their rite, and Circus stage bodies.
  - **The shell:** for `PuppetStringsRules.UNSPOOL_TICKS` (12) the body has no AI or gravity, is invulnerable, has its own tick cancelled and is skipped by every active-puppet count. Taut strings haul it up 1.6 blocks as it shrinks, twists and peels into sinew, and a flash covers the rest before removal.
  - **State and visuals:** the countdown lives in persistent data, so it survives a save. Visual timing never gates gameplay. Death and Peaceful despawn are unchanged.
- **Morphling interference:** With an equipped Morphling, every qualifying same-owner shaped puppet or Commandeered Will operates at **75%** of its ordinary skill-adjusted tether range and pays `ceil(post–Thread Economy upkeep × 1.5)` at its existing one-minute transaction. Payment remains atomic; failure uses the ordinary unravel path and grants nothing. Successful modified payment refreshes the equipped Morphling's existing fed timer without granting bonding, maturity, husbandry, borrowed blood, or Thelemic reserve progress. Multiple puppets each pay their own surcharge but do not stack the range or Morphling blood multiplier. Gnawed tethers render with dark intermittent gaps, the Crossbar reports `Gnawed — 75% range, 150% upkeep`, and contextual Summons values show the effective range and upkeep. Summon/call cost, capacity, health, damage, and active caps are unchanged.
- **Anti-stockpile rule:** active summon cap is calculated from the player's `skill_puppet_skein` level and checks active bound summons by owner, not by crossbar. Carrying extra crossbars cannot exceed the learned cap. Silent Archon's configured bonus expands the combined cap for **claimed Wills only**; learned artificial shapes still obey the ordinary shaped-body cap, so claiming a Will first cannot consume an unused shaped slot and shapes cannot occupy Will-only bonus slots. If an older unloaded body returns after a replacement filled the cap, loaded tethers are reconciled deterministically by original binding time and overflow bodies unravel.
- **Skills:** `skill_puppet_skein` increases the player-wide active cap; `skill_living_sinew` increases health/damage; `skill_far_tether` adds 8 blocks of tether range per level; `skill_thread_economy` reduces call/upkeep charge by 5% per level to a 70% floor; `skill_bound_command` adds 32 capacity, 4 tether-range blocks, and 20 ticks of unequipped grace per level; and toggleable Degree 6 **High-Strung** accelerates melee puppets, extends command range, and raises both Thread and blood upkeep, with recoil when a strained puppet dies.
- **Harbinger UI:** `HarbingerProgressScreen` includes a `SUMMONS` tab. It groups summons by degree, shows degree-locked, recipe-locked, trial-required, and known states, reports base and skill-modified stats, and creates a client-only preview entity for the selected summon. Preview render failures fall back to an icon/text placeholder rather than crashing the screen.
- **Puppet appearance:** All eight registered shapes have dedicated geometry and UV-fitted pixel-art atlases, with embedded textures in their editable Blockbench files. The Ringmaster Pattern has its own `ringmaster_pattern` entity type, conductor model, regalia texture, and sparse command-thread glow; the old conversion of a Ringmaster saved under the shared `mnemonist_puppet` type was deleted on 2026-11-07 (the mod is not live). Preview entities retain their selected summon name so this distinction also appears in the Summons tab. Blood Curs share the Hound mesh with a brighter blood-only texture variant; bone and iron retain their authored colors. The rigs use 128px atlases. The standard Cinder Bellows uses its authored palette and maps every face at one pixel per model unit. Its sparse ember glow banks at rest and flares through the breath. The standard Mnemonist Puppet also maps each face at one pixel per model unit. Its jointed bisque body has three modelled crimson control lines. `MnemonistThreadLayer` draws another three to five tapered HutosLib tendrils from the animated spool, with a faint pulsing glow and travelling curvature waves that react to walking, strikes, Encore, hurt and death. Encore also opens the jaw and spins the spool. Control threads from the owner's Crossbar hand, Vesper, or a Blood Drunk Puppeteer to each body are tapered Animus strands, the same surface as the Hematic Command tether, with a bead of blood riding out along them; an equipped Morphling chews gaps that crawl along the thread. The assets are built by the git-tracked `tools/circus/` scripts (`puppet_rig.py` and one `build_*.py` per body) and checked by `tools/circus/verify_troupe_assets.py`; the older notes in `tools/oneoff/PUPPET_ASSETS.md` are local and untracked.

Each degree grant and login recovery awards both the corresponding component crafting recipe and Cardinal Ordeal recipe. Trial bosses reuse the summon definitions as unbound hostile versions with default boss tuning: 1.5x health, 1.25x damage, no owner/crossbar upkeep, no active-summon cap accounting, and unlock credit only when the active rite's caster, summon name, and tracked entity UUID all match the death event.

Current summon definitions:

| Summon | Degree | Role | Base HP | Base Damage | Call Charge | Charge/min | Trial Blood |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `veinwing_vulture` | 3 | Fast flying striker | 14 | 4 | 28 | 18/min | 500 |
| `marrow_spitter` | 3 | Hovering three-dagger juggler | 22 | 5 | 38 | 12/min | 750 |
| `gorebound_hulk` | 4 | Slow heavy bruiser | 55 | 9 | 56 | 8/min | 1100 |
| `scarlet_mummer` | 4 | Attention controller | 24 | 3 | 48 | 14/min | 950 |
| `ringmaster_pattern` | 4 | Conductor | 28 | 1 | 52 | 14/min | none (no Cardinal Ordeal) |
| `sanguine_hound` | 4 | Pursuit harrier | 30 | 6 | 44 | 15/min | 850 |
| `cinder_bellows` | 4 | Telegraphing fire cone | 30 | 4 | 48 | 16/min | 900 |
| `mnemonist_puppet` | 5 | Memory echo specialist | 26 | 3 | 64 | 16/min | 1400 |

`marrow_spitter` retains its Skeleton-based save and registry identity as the Marrow Juggler. It never burns in sunlight or equips a bow. Three non-pickable daggers follow a 35-tick volley, share the former Blood Shot's rounded velocity-based impact budget, and retain Blood Loss. Armor still mitigates each separate strike. Friendly bodies, Blood Curs and teacher demonstrations are excluded. The regular puppet wears comedy and tragedy masks on a shared yoke above a split crimson coat. Six jointed arms catch and pass three daggers in a staggered cascade, with a throwing-hand flick on each projectile release. The Chamber true self has its own three-mask rig and ordeal animations. Both bound and trial forms retain the hovering orbit rather than pursuing with melee.

`mnemonist_puppet` is the bounded V1 memory-replay summon. It records up to six recent damage memories against its current target, drops stale memories after 160 ticks, and every 40 ticks can replay one as reduced, capped magic damage as crimson threads lash from its spool to the target (the `MNEMONIC_REPLAY` Animus visual) with red/pale Hemomancy glows. Replay damage is marked so it cannot record itself, and the implementation intentionally avoids full action replay. Only the Mnemonist shape replays: the Ringmaster Pattern Conductor never records or replays memories. Damage capture checks the server's tracked live Mnemonists rather than searching the world on every hit.

`scarlet_mummer` draws hostile attention and survives through evasive movement rather than adding another damage role. `sanguine_hound` is a fast pursuit body that ruptures below 40% health into three to five short-lived Blood Curs. Those curs inherit pursuit ownership only: they consume no Crossbar capacity or upkeep, do not persist, and grant no refund when they expire.

### 17.1 Circus Integration Boundary

The physical Acrobat, Fire Breather, Dagger Thrower and Stilt Walker use articulated native meshes from their editable Blockbench projects (2026-11-20). The per-face UVs retain one texel per unit. Walking, resting, performance and defense poses follow the existing entity state, with animated cloth, articulated held props, and Crossbar thread origins at the posed right hand. The shared performer render path still selects the entity's two costume variants, and the Chamber true selves have their own render path. See [Circus](CIRCUS.md#physical-performers-2026-11-20) for the exporter.


The Crimson Troupe (Circus) is the primary Puppeteering teaching sub-faction, adjacent to the Brined Court. It reuses the Marionette Crossbar, Puppeteer's Spindle, summon definitions, Cardinal Ordeals, command radial, Living Staff forms, and shared summon lifecycle. It must not introduce a second summon registry, ownership capability, upkeep currency, command surface, or progression ladder.

The school teaches seven ordinary artificial bodies through personal instruction, existing Cardinal Ordeals and server-observed practicals. `cinder_bellows` adds a Degree 4 coiled fire-breathing body; `marrow_spitter` retains its IDs as the Marrow Juggler. `scarlet_mummer` remains the attention-control anchor. Scarlet Serpents and Prism Cuttles remain natural animals whose warning displays and chromatophores inform Circus presentation; they are not faction agents or additional artificial summon definitions. Two jarred Prism Cuttles in the pavilion make that influence visible without moving their ecology into the Circus.

The physical Circus pavilion is a world-generated location rather than a runtime event that can overwrite an established player build. Its placement must reject wet, obstructed, or sharply uneven footprints. Layered presentation is viewer-specific, but collision, hostile entities, rewards, discovery, and progression remain server-authoritative. The presentation is the perception overlay only (`CircusPerceptionOverlay`: silhouettes, cloth, diamonds). Since 2026-11-15 (D-29, PT-57; chunk 15 T8 and T12) the pavilion has two real galleries with stairs for every player, and the Ringmaster's box on the upper one is reached on foot from the floor. Acclimation changes only the look, as a phantom show on the pavilion's own marks (2026-11-16): a Disturbed visitor catches fragments (a seated figure that hides from a direct look, a still figure on a trapeze, dead bulbs); an Acclimating one sees a third of the seats filled and one act rehearsing under a sweeping spotlight; an Attuned one sits in a full phantom audience before trapeze artists and a ring act under steady string lights and spotlights, with the house gone dark. A ruined pavilion shows only the fragments. An Unaware visitor sees the galleries bare.

The finale is gated since 2026-11-15 (D-30, D-31, NQ-15-5, NQ-15-6 B; `CircusRouteRules.pactGate`): a Harbinger needs Degree 4 and any one school report; a player whose Unstained state blocks Harbinger progress may begin it on The Missing Understudy report and no Degree, and may only kill him at the kneel (Liberation), never absorb him. The gate is checked again at the finale, and the Ringmaster's greeting names what is missing.

Acts (D-37, D-38, NQ-15-8 A, NQ-15-9 A; since 2026-11-15): each taught body has one act, fired from the Act entry on the Crossbar radial's inner ring through `PacketPuppetAct` (rate-limited) and performed by the selected shape's nearest body: Mummer Spotlight, Vulture Trapeze, Juggler Feint, Bellows Smoke, Mnemonist Encore, Hound Scent, Hulk Lift. The Ringmaster Pattern's act is Ring: every body of the owner within 32 blocks performs its act at once. Starting thread costs and cooldowns are in `PuppetAct` (6 to 10 thread, 12 to 30 s; Ring 30 thread, 60 s) and are tuned in play; thread is spent only when an act is performed. Acts are not strands. The Pattern still costs no slot of the cap and is called at the Spindle; the transposition ring no longer offers it.

At Degree 3 the Mnemonist's Circus card is a teaser: it names the Circus and the open country its camps keep to (plains, forests, taiga, savanna and badlands) and offers no Waybill. At Degree 4, the Vicar refers curious players to the Mnemonist, who already offers the Scarlet Waybill and the Circus introduction. The Waybill seeks an abandoned stage (tag `troupe_abandoned_stage_targets`) while the Retired Understudy's testimony is given and the stage record unread, unless the player sneaks; otherwise the next untaught professor's camp, and sneaking the nearest unfinished pavilion. A pavilion whose Ringmaster was destroyed is vacant and the Waybill passes it by (D-32, PT-58, PT-62). Finding the pavilion completes the optional Side ledger entry, including when the visit predates the referral. It does not require either finale or affect the next degree.

Circus location observation and passive acclimation require a living, non-spectator player inside a registered pavilion piece. Ordinary early discovery remains valid at D0 with inactive blood. Dead or spectator ticks retain previously earned discovery/acclimation without adding either and synchronize perception as outside; they do not reset routes, challenges or completed outcomes.

The playable pavilion route uses per-player acclimation (0-1000), four controlled-real acts, the finale in his Chamber and a site-global first-completion claim. Since 2026-11-18 no route is chosen before the fight: the route reads `NEUTRAL` until the finale ends, then `SUCCESSION_COMPLETE` or `LIBERATION_COMPLETE`, and the ending is chosen at his kneel (see the finale paragraph below). Acclimation comes from passive exposure (1 point per 80 living, non-spectator ticks inside a pavilion) and one-time milestones: 50 for the first talk with each of the eight performer roles, 100 for An Empty Ring, 100 per practical, 150 each for The Wrong Audience and The Missing Understudy, 150 for the attention act and 100 for each of acts 2 to 4. The challenge bits (`CircusRouteRules`) are bit 0 the attention act and bits 2 to 4 the doll, knife and carousel acts; bit 1 (the old route choice) is retired. The finale opens once the attention act is done and the gate is open. Absorbing him at the kneel (Succession) needs 1000 acclimation, the attention act and all three acts (`SUCCESSION_CHALLENGES`), active blood and not Unstained; it takes his office as a low-damage Conductor pattern. Killing him (Liberation) needs nothing more: the ruin is laid over the pavilion, the real captives (the three failed initiates bound atop the carousel horses) are freed and the troupe leaves. The captives can no longer be cut by hand or by Thread Ripper, and the carousel takes no blows. Thread Ripper is Liberation's reward, a Summa memory most Liberators cannot learn yet, so it usually arrives as the memory item. Neither ending checks Degree or school work (D-30). Both endings award the cosmetic Ringmaster's Topper. The Topper, and the Thread Ripper memory when Liberation cannot teach it, are the `PendingDelivery` claim `circus_finale_rewards`: the exact owed count is kept in the `CircusProgress` attachment (it survives death), delivered only to a living player outside an observational Chamber visit, counted by actual insertion, and retried on the one-second driver, login and respawn. The act in progress (challenge, held ticks, origin, the attention spider) also lives in `CircusProgress`: it survives a relog and is cleared on death. The perception overlay is the `CIRCUS_PROGRESS` row of `PlayerStateSync`: lifecycle sends start outside, and acclimation or inside-state changes raise a dirty flag flushed once at the end of the tick, so nothing is broadcast per second.

The Side Assignment Ledger tracks An Empty Ring, seven faculty practicals, The Wrong Audience, The Missing Understudy and repeat guest acts. Instruction requires active blood, the shape's degree and a nearby living professor outside combat. Existing known shapes retain use and satisfy instruction, while practical and reward flags remain separate. Guest payment is four Enthralling Filaments once per Minecraft day across the whole school (one `guest.day` key read from `getDayTime`, not one per professor), with exact saved overflow collected from a Threadkeeper. Rehearsal targets are local, temporary and give no loot or XP. Safe stage demonstrations have no player owner or trial identity and bypass combat, upkeep and active-cap reconciliation.

The finale in his Chamber (owner, 2026-11-18; `common/encounter/ordeal/finale/`, full design in [CIRCUS.md](CIRCUS.md) "The finale in his Chamber"). It is begun from his dialogue at the real pavilion and fought on a copy of the pavilion in his Chamber of Will (`FinaleStage`, `RingmasterFinaleDirector`); the crossing is hidden under his 60-tick opening, and while the owner is inside the real Ringmaster, troupe and carousel are frozen and untouchable (another speaker is told he is elsewhere). His real Chamber render is projected onto the tent's own block faces outside the ring, nearly opaque at the opening and thinning as he is worn down until the tent's stripes show through, with stage lights, a phantom audience in the seats and the true selves of the professors this player has passed at their stations. Phase 1 (100% to 50% health): from the rafters he throws a volley with two fake copies (a hit bursts a fake; only his knives are real) and then drops to a low perch, and uses the arena (string lights that root, a burning spotlight, an audience rush, the carousel firing its horses, spiralling them out and slamming its pole). Phase 2: he leaps down in his true self and walks the ring (staff strike, carousel swing, an echo cue calling one passed professor's signature ordeal move, and two moves only a blood charge allows); bat swarms steal the player's blood through `BloodAccounting` and carry it to him as that charge. The blow that would kill him makes him kneel: the owner's own blow kills him (Liberation), held Blood Absorption takes his place (Succession, refused without its requirements). The ending is laid on the real site on return through `CircusFinaleSettlement.apply`; after Succession the real Ringmaster is retired on his perch, still the trade speaker and conductor teacher. A killing blow on the player is caught and throws them out with nothing dropped, releasing the site. Every move is a `BossMoveTimeline` with a bold floor telegraph and a fast blow; every number is the builder's call. The old real-world finale (RAFTERS, CAROUSEL and DESCENT on the real site, the anchors, Sleight, Knife Board, the Cue, Strings Cut and the yield and collapse beats) is deleted. The Circus sound events (`entity.circus_ringmaster.phase_change`, `.finale_collapse`, `.hurt`, `entity.impaled_procession.thread_sever`, `.anchor_break`, `entity.circus_performer.windup`) play the six cue candidates until the owner picks; `entity.circus_ringmaster.music` has no track yet.

Fight and school rules (2026-11-14): a blow from a body the site owner holds (a non-trial bound puppet, a Blood Cur, their projectiles, the Mnemonist Puppet's replay) counts as the owner's on the Ringmaster, performers and carousel. During an act or finale the troupe's strikes and area attacks land only on the owner and the owner's bodies, through `ManipulationCombatHelper.canHarmFor`; the finale stays solo and a bystander who strikes the troupe is told so on the action bar (D-34). Thread Ripper does not disrupt or unravel Vesper's encounter bodies (D-35). A practical or guest act is refused in Peaceful and ends with the retry line when Peaceful is set or fewer rehearsal threats live than it needs (two for the Mummer and the Bellows, one for the rest; PT-59, PT-63). A refused claim says whether the ring is busy, the site settled, or the visitor has no route (PT-61). The guest-pay ledger line says one guest act a day for the whole school (D-45).

Three kinds of template ship, all `hemomancy:circus_pavilion` structures on the `#hemomancy:has_structure/circus_pavilion` biome tag: the 81x23x65 pavilion (`crimson_troupe_pavilion.nbt`, with the Strongman's and the Beast Tamer's side rings since 2026-11-16, written by `tools/worldgen/circus_sites.py` from the site kit since 2026-11-15, set `circus_pavilion` at spacing 48/separation 16), five 27x12x27 camps with five faculty variants (set `troupe_teaching_camps`, 24/8), and the 17x10x15 abandoned stage that holds the Missing Understudy's stage record (`troupe_abandoned_stages`, 32/10); all three written by the generator since 2026-11-15. Sites bring their own ground (`beard_box`; the camps and stage also carry a foundation skirt under row 1). Placement (D-43, 2026-11-15) samples the laid-out footprint's corners, edge midpoints and a grid 8 blocks apart, wants every sampled column dry and under height 150 and all of them within 6 blocks of each other, samples only the pavilion's centred 43-block core (its side rings and yards sit on whatever ground is there), keeps every site 6 chunks from a village start, and keeps camps and stages 6 chunks from a pavilion cell (`StructurePlacementChecks`, `TroupeFootprintScan`). On three measured seeds the nearest pavilion was 653, 1,968 and 3,064 blocks away (`circusValidationServer`). Normal Waybill use locates the next eligible untaught professor; sneak-use searches for an unfinished pavilion. The search never runs on the server thread: the Waybill says it is searching, `CircusWaybillSearch` runs `StructureSitePrediction` (each set's potential chunk per spacing cell, its placement check, vanilla's weighted pick among the set's structures and that structure's own generation point, with no chunk loads) on the background worker pool, bounded to 32 spacing cells each way, and records the target when the answer lands on the server thread. A finished nearest pavilion gives way to the nearest unfinished one within 2,560 blocks. One search runs per player at a time; the per-cell predictions are cached for the session. The Relay Chart's `CourtSeatSearch` shares the same per-player and cache state through `common/util/OffThreadSearch`. New faculty do not join the old four-performer finale requirements. Both existing endings, their rewards and the lethal captive outcome remain unchanged. See [the detailed school contract](archive/tracks/circus/03-puppetry-and-circus-mechanics.md).

Pavilion generation checks the selected stub's allowed biome before validating its footprint, avoiding terrain scans for ocean candidates. The corners are asked first, so a wet or steep side is refused after a few columns, and the whole gate asks at most a few dozen columns, not every column. The ocean-travel and vanilla locate profiles and validation evidence are recorded in [PELAGIC_WORLDGEN.md](PELAGIC_WORLDGEN.md).

Faculty appearance: Strongman, Beast Tamer, Threadkeeper and Retired Understudy use dedicated humanoid models on `CircusFacultyModel`, each with two accent variants. During SETUP/PERFORM the Threadkeeper inspects a ledger as its spindle turns, the Understudy lowers a half-mask, the Strongman presses a barbell and the Beast Tamer cracks a whip. These are client visuals only.

Performer threads: every Circus performer and faculty member strings its puppets from its right hand with the same Animus thread players use. This covers teaching demonstration bodies and the Enthralled Dolls raised when a performer is attacked. Demonstration bodies sync their teacher as owner; existing saved bodies are backfilled on their next stage tick. Their cancelled tick still bypasses ownership, upkeep and combat. Because they now have an owner, they no longer despawn in Peaceful.

The Circus site kit (chunk 15 T7, NQ-15-1 A, built 2026-11-15) is the set every rebuilt site will be made from: king and quarter poles by section, a ring curb and its bend round a sawdust ring, seating tiers, gallery rails, a trapeze and a safety net that lets through 20% of fall damage, a scalloped valance, guy stakes, the Ringmaster's two-tall podium, crimson footlights (light 12), Crossbar rigs, a Spindle rack, trophies, a pelt drape, the procession plinth, painted wagon panels on two-block wagon wheels, a cook pot, costume racks, trunks that do not open, a ticket window, pennant lines, and one apparatus per camp (knife wheel and target board, stilt rack and weight frame, ember pit, bellows stand and hound hoop, prompt-book table). Striped and laced canvas, a lacquered wainscot and ring sawdust are its surfaces. The four evidence records are now distinct objects: a stage bill, a loft rigging log, a quarters ledger and a carousel maker's plate. None of the kit drops anything. The camps and the stage are built on the kit since 2026-11-15 (chunk 15 T9): each camp a yard of ring sawdust on its own skirt, ringed by a low bank, with a practice ring for its professors, the Threadkeeper's lean-to with the Spindle, a painted wagon, lamp posts and its discipline's apparatus north of the ring; the stage a burnt wagon wreck by a rutted road with the stage bill on its split boards.

The pavilion (chunk 15 T8, built 2026-11-15) is the kit's first site. Its big top is an octagon of laced and striped canvas on a wainscot, 43 by 39, under a stepped canvas roof; two king poles stand in the ring curb, and the Impaled Procession turns on its plinth in a sawdust ring of radius 7 with six crimson footlights. The lower (north) gallery, the loft, has its deck at height 5 and holds the loft rigging log; the upper (south) gallery has its deck at height 7 and the Ringmaster's box built out from it over the ring. Each gallery has stairs at both ends, so a survival player walks from the floor to the Ringmaster's side and talks to him there. Seating banks face the ring from north and south, rigging towers with trapeze and net stand at the east and west ends, and outside are the midway (ticket booth, banner line, the Threadkeeper's stall), the backyard (three painted wagons, the cookhouse, the dressing tent with the Understudy and the quarters ledger) and the Strongman's and Beast Tamer's yards. The template places all ten actors, its three records, 30 hung Hematic Lanterns and three Abocipher emitters (Harbinger Outpost profile); no cell under its roof is dark enough to spawn a monster, which the generator checks.

Site outcomes and gifts (D-44, NQ-15-10, chunk 15 T11, built 2026-11-15): no Circus site holds an openable container. A Liberation lays the ruin over the pavilion: the roof torn open in three places with canvas heaped below, the plinth and ring splintered, the trapezes fallen on their chains, the nets torn, the box's valance down, a third of the lanterns and half the footlights gone; the finale performers still standing leave, the faculty stay and teach. A Succession hangs the successor's banner behind the Ringmaster's podium, and his greeting names the holder to other visitors. `CircusSiteStateService` lays either overlay one loaded chunk at a time, saves the chunks still owed on the site, and changes a cell only while it still holds the pavilion's own block. Each professor gives two Enthralling Filaments and one frame material for their body once, on the first passed practical with them, owed through the `OwedRewards` `PendingDelivery` claim before the practical is recorded; a full pack or a death keeps it owed.

The five teaching camps use red-and-ivory A-frame canvas tents with peaked roofs and open entrances toward the practice yard. Separate tent decks join a narrow boardwalk, worn dirt paths and practice courts with clipped corners. Lantern posts, benches and specialty props furnish the camp: aerial rigging, knife targets, Strongman weights and masks, fire practice supplies, or the Understudy's books and records. Faculty, Spindles and existing clue blocks keep their original positions. Changed templates appear only in newly generated chunks; the mod is not live, so older generated camps need no upkeep.

Cinder Bellows: D4, 30 HP, base attack 4, speed .24, call 48, upkeep 16/minute; frame ordeal 900 mL Dominion Lesser. Its 20/40/40-tick cycle produces four two-base-damage fire pulses in a five-block, sixty-degree cone, with obstruction and ally checks and no terrain ignition. The Marrow Juggler shares the previous rounded projectile impact over three sequential daggers every 35 ticks; since 2026-11-15 it is a pin body (D-39, NQ-15-7 A): the third dagger of a volley pins the target 30 ticks and no dagger causes Blood Loss. The Hulk retains its strength and adds a strike wind-up.

The Bellows presentation uses an eleven-joint coil that curls behind a rising S-curved trunk; pale belly scutes run unbroken to the sternum and the free tail tip lifts and curls. Four pairs of ribs wrap the flanks around two pleated bellows lobes that inflate on the draw. The skull has a brow ridge, cheekbones, snout and hinged jaw; a folded hood, crimson ruff, wrist-mounted wick torch and marionette fittings complete the Fire Breather's puppet. The standard rig is baked from the Blockbench project in `docs/art/cinder_bellows/`. It rears back and hauls its elbows back while inhaling, then lunges the neck forward, opens the jaw and pumps its arms through the breath, with the head countering the lunge so the mouth stays aimed down the cone. A sparse ember glow in the eyes, bellows, throat and torch banks at rest and flares with the breath. The breath itself is drawn client-side with the Flammeus thermal flames (a directed jet of licks that burn out into smoke), with banked wisps during the inhale. The standard renderer emits the flames from the posed mouth along the server-synced breath direction. Travel curvature propagates through the tail while its underside remains grounded. Rebuild only these model assets with `tools/circus/build_cinder_bellows.py`; `tools/circus/preview_cinder_bellows.py --serve` opens an authoring preview with idle, slither and breath poses. The `bellows` scene in `runCircusReviewClient` captures the standard rig through its breath cycle.

The Juggler presentation uses a hunched torso and hood carrying angled laughing, mourning and blank masks. All six arms have connected shoulders, elbows, wrists and fingers; three whole knives arc between the actual bent hands, with staggered catch times. Separate robe panels and a central sash sway over a split, ragged hem. Its repainted 128px crimson, ivory and iron atlas is embedded in the editable Blockbench source. Rebuild these assets alone with `tools/circus/build_marrow_juggler.py`; `tools/circus/preview_marrow_juggler.py --serve` supplies a textured comparison with travel and scrubbed juggling poses. This revision preserves the existing summon identity, attack cadence and damage. Native-client appearance remains unverified.

The physical Hulk uses the Blockbench project in `docs/art/gorebound_hulk/` and its 256 by 128 atlas at one texel per model unit. A barrel chest and raised back frame a low carved skull, while stitched forearms carry iron bands and bone knuckles. Striped trunks, a lifting belt and iron-capped boots mark it as the Strongman's puppet. The chest shifts with the walk, the knees bend and the ankles compensate for the stride. The synced strike windup raises both fists before the swing carries them down together. Run `tools/circus/build_gorebound_hulk.py` to bake the project into the Java mesh and runtime assets. `tools/circus/preview_gorebound_hulk.py --serve` opens the idle, walk and strike authoring preview.

### 17.2 Rogue Hemomancer Wills

Rogue Hemomancer Wills are late-Harbinger ambushers keyed to the player's blood temper rather than ordinary biome spawns. The system uses one data-driven `will` entity with two origins: **Broken** Wills use fixed tier stats forever, while **Sent** Wills snapshot scaled stats from the target player when spawned. Wills cast their curated school kits through `WillManipulationCaster`, `ManipulationCastContext`, and the `EntityCastableManipulation` path, so their combat uses mob-safe versions of the same projectile, fire, ice, light, death, and shadow manipulation fantasies the player uses. `DrudgeAction` and `MobManipCaster` remain Drudge infrastructure only.

Broken Wills cycle through their kit with occasional stutters, selling incomplete former-Harbinger Thelemic memory. Sent Wills (60 / 90 / 120 HP and 8 / 10 / 12 damage at D6 / D7 / D8 against a 20 HP target, `WillCombatRules.sentStats`, NQ-06-6) use a small priority controller instead: they prefer mobility at range, defensive casts when injured, close-range pressure when the target is inside melee space, and finishers or burst casts when the target is vulnerable.

Lux and Tenebris Will kits now mirror the player's improved combat style verbs. Lux Wills open with `hematic_flare`, then escalate into `prismatic_reproof`, `hematic_beacon`, and `unclosing_eye`; Tenebris Wills keep `void_shroud` and `umbral_step`, but add `gloam_laceration` before the wider `blood_eclipse` cone. Temper weapon/manipulation counter checks special-case Wills by their synced school, so Lux attacks dynamically oppose Tenebris-school Wills and Tenebris attacks dynamically oppose Lux-school Wills instead of relying only on static entity-type tags.

Wills also spawn with visible, non-drop living weapons through `WillEquipmentRules`. Tier-I Broken Wills carry a `living_staff`; Tier-II+ Broken Wills and all Sent Wills carry temper weapons: Animus blade, Flammeus torch, Ductilis crossbow, Lux spear, Mortem sickle, Congeatio flail, Ferric axe and Tenebris baghnakh. `WillWeaponController` supplies mob-safe weapon pressure without invoking player inventory or blood-volume hooks: torches burn, flails slow, crossbows fire blood bolts, claws/bladework bleed, Ferric Wills guard and knock back, and school weapons reinforce the Will's combat identity.

Ambient ambushes are driven by `WillAmbushDirector` and `WillAmbushState`. Eligible active-blood Harbingers at the configured minimum degree roll on a cooldown, with chance multipliers from ripe/dark terrain, Qliphoth bloom ownership, Blood Moon, Blood Drunkenness, Fungal Whisper herald windows, and hidden hive attention. Founding Fanes, the Chamber of Will, and placed Harbinger Outpost pieces are sanctuary exclusions through `WillSanctuaryRules`.

Successful ambushes spawn a `will_anchor` first. All nearby players receive a short sound/overlay cue through `WillPresenceCuePacket`. Oculiflora carriers get the stronger counterplay: `WillAnchorRenderer` renders the pre-materialization anchor only when `OculifloraReticularisItem.networkSightActive(localPlayer)` is true. After the anchor lifetime expires, it materializes the composed group and may replace the first Broken slot with a `blood_drunk_puppeteer`, making the Puppeteer part of the Will archetype without replacing its existing combat identity.

Wills dissolve instead of using ordinary corpse loot. Dissolve rewards are school-keyed through `WillCombatRules.lootFor`: the matching representative enzyme always drops, and Broken Wills have a small `faded_memory` chance. Sent Will dissolution increments hidden hive attention on the targeted player only; no Apotheos or progression gate is attached to that pressure in this stage.

Broken Wills enter their short bindable falter window when one player deals enough burst damage: by default, 25% of max health within 80 ticks. Non-player damage does not build pressure, mixed players do not pool pressure, and the meter resets when the burst window expires or a different player takes over. Sent Wills never falter. Blood Absorption does not affect Wills by default, but channeling it near a faltering Broken Will resolves Absorb: the channel latches the Will into `ABSORBING`, freezes AI/casting/weapon pressure, and advances a separate absorption-progress meter instead of draining health. Bare Blood Absorption advances the struggle steadily; Living Staff absorption advances faster and scales through Vascular Draw, Hematic Focus, awakened Vesper memory, and Vesper's Refusal. Completing the staged struggle immediately consumes and removes the Will: it grants +3 alignment toward its school, rolls the absorption enzyme/faded-memory reward chance at that moment, emits the final black-glow pulse, and does not enter a second dissolve phase or use ordinary dissolve loot. If the channel is dropped past the grace window, the Will snaps back to `MATERIALIZED` in controlled rage: it restores to at least 40% max health, targets the absorber, suppresses immediate refaltering, and resumes pressure. This Will-specific absorption draw uses small black glow motes pulled toward the active hand or staff instead of the normal blood-cell siphon particles, with a second spiral of the Will's school-colored motes wrapping inward along the same pull; the Will shell flickers during `ABSORBING` as the channel approaches completion. Blood Projection aimed at a faltering Broken Will resolves the new Redirect-as-banishment path: it spends projection blood, bursts the Will into a particle cloud, subtracts 3 alignment from that school, and dissolves it without turning it into a temporary ally. Right-click behavior is now reserved for **Commandeer** with an owner-attuned Marionette Crossbar; an unattuned or foreign Crossbar is rejected before falter/backfire resolution. Commandeer spends 56 Crossbar charge (28 for a Silent Archon), clears the Will's former target, counts the claimed Will against the player-wide puppeteer cap, and gives that body a base 16-charge-per-minute upkeep before Thread Economy. It then follows the same equipped-Crossbar grace, hostile focus, per-body starvation, persistence, Peaceful exemption, and dimension-severance rules as shaped summons. Silent Archon players also receive the configured `claimedWillBonusCapSilentArchon` bonus, whose extra slots are reserved for claimed Wills.

Legacy summon/test entities (`enthralled_doll`, `wretched_will`, and `blood_thrall`) remain mechanically unchanged by this pass.

## 18. Drudge System

**Status:** `WIP — post-alpha`. The implementation is retained for development and later expansion work, but Drudges are not part of the first-release gameplay promise. The Drudge Electrode, Drudge Submission Device, and Semi-Sentient Construct are isolated in the Hemomancy WIP creative tab and the SSC is omitted from the core Materials Atlas. The persistent entity, birthing/refill loop, memory execution spine, direct-routing tender behavior, rogue-state rules, and interaction controls remain available for testing.

The Drudge is a persistent, player-owned semi-organic construct that holds a single **Blood Memory** (`BloodManipulation`) and executes it autonomously within a leash radius anchored to a **Semi-Sentient Construct (SSC)** block. Unlike the Blood Thrall (a transient courier), the Drudge is a long-term servant that "learns a job" and keeps doing it.

### Entity: `DrudgeEntity`

- **Class:** `common/entity/npc/DrudgeEntity`
- **Registry ID:** `hemomancy:drudge`
- **Extends:** `PathfinderMob implements OwnableEntity`

**Synched data (server→client):**
| Field | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `DATA_OWNER_UUID` | `Optional<UUID>` | UUID of the Harbinger who birthed this Drudge |
| `DATA_HOME_POS` | `Optional<BlockPos>` | World position of the bound SSC |
| `DATA_BLOOD_CHARGE` | `float` | Current internal blood reserve (0–3 000 mL) |
| `DATA_IS_ROGUE` | `boolean` | Whether the Drudge has turned hostile |
| `DATA_PASSIVE_MODE` | `boolean` | Passive = auto-fires; Commanded = electrode-only |

**Attributes:**
- Health: 20 HP, Speed: 0.22, Armor: 4, Attack: 3, Follow Range: 32

**Blood economy:** The Drudge has an internal blood pool (`bloodCharge`, max 3 000 mL). The SSC refills it at 50 mL/tick when the Drudge is within 3 blocks of the SSC. The Drudge does **not** draw from the player's `IBloodVolume` cap in real time.

**Direct routing tender behavior:** Drudges near their SSC scan nearby saved Suture links every 40 ticks and can feed linked machines through `DrudgeTenderSource`. A successful tender action spends 20 internal blood charge, respects the linked source contract and target request, and does not create blood or act as bulk storage.

**Action cost:** Each manipulation fires at `cost × DRUDGE_ACTION_COST_MULTIPLIER` (default 1.5×) and a cooldown of `cooldown × DRUDGE_COOLDOWN_MULTIPLIER` (default 2×).

### AI Goal Stack

| Priority | Goal | Condition |
|----------|------|-----------|
| 1 | `DrudgeReturnToSSCGoal` | Blood charge below threshold OR outside leash range |
| 2 | `DrudgeExecuteMemoryGoal` | Has memory + sufficient charge + (Passive or electrode signal) |
| 3 | `MeleeAttackGoal` | Rogue mode only |
| 4 | `WaterAvoidingRandomStrollGoal` | Not rogue, within leash range |
| 5 | `RandomLookAroundGoal` | Always |

### Drudge Memory Behavior

`DrudgeExecuteMemoryGoal` dispatches the installed manipulation's registered `DrudgeAction` from `ManipulationInit`. Actions use the Drudge's current block position as the work origin and `drudgeWorkRadius` as the search radius. Blood charge and cooldown are only consumed when the action returns `true`; unsupported or unregistered actions do not fire. A Drudge's hostiles are the monsters its owner may harm (`ManipulationCombatHelper.canHarmFor`): its owner's puppets, pets and allies are spared, and a Drudge whose owner is away falls back to team and vanilla `canAttack` (G-2b, 2026-11-13).

| `deadly_gaze` | Lifts, grips and heavily strikes the nearest hostile for 2× the Drudge's attack damage |

| `cauterizing_rebuke` | Cleanses Poison, Wither and Necrosis from the Drudge, then sears nearby hostiles (2 fire damage, Searing 5 s) |
| `scalding_updraft` | Launches the Drudge upward on hot air |
| `void_shroud` | Veils the Drudge (30 s) until it attacks |
| `gloam_laceration` | Slashes the nearest hostile from darkness: 3.5 magic damage, 6 while the Drudge is invisible or in darkness, plus Blood Loss (7 s) on a landed hit |
| `blood_eclipse` | Obscures and damages hostiles near the Drudge: 1.2× its attack damage and Obscured (5 s) |
| `hemorrhage` | Afflicts the nearest hostile with Necrosis (5 s) |
| `insatiable_hunger` | Curses the nearest hostile with anti-healing hunger (Insatiable Hunger, 11 s) |
| `grave_debt` | Marks the nearest hostile to burst at low health for the Drudge's owner; the owner gets no blood back, as the mark cost them nothing |
| `exsanguinate` | Drains the nearest hostile for 20% of its max health as magic damage and heals the Drudge for half |
| `crimson_tithe` | Unsupported; cannot be used by Drudges |
| `unclosing_eye` | Unsupported; cannot be used by Drudges |
| `bloom_of_rot` | Unsupported; cannot be used by Drudges |
| `endless_hour` | Unsupported; cannot be used by Drudges |

Every other active manipulation registers `DrudgeAction.DRUDGE_UNSUPPORTED` and never fires from a Drudge. Hostile-targeting actions pick `Monster`s only.

### Rogue State

A Drudge goes Rogue when:
1. Blood charge reaches 0 and it cannot reach its SSC within `DRUDGE_ROGUE_TIMEOUT_TICKS` (default 200 ticks = 10 s).
2. It drifts more than `leashRadius + 6` blocks from its SSC home.

In Rogue state: targets players (priority) then monsters; the equipped memory is **dropped on death** so it is not lost.

### Interaction Summary

| Action | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Right-click Drudge (empty hand) | Toggle Passive/Commanded mode + status readout |
| Right-click Drudge (with Blood Memory) | Install the memory |
| Shift+right-click Drudge (empty hand) | Retrieve installed memory |
| DSD shift+right-click on Drudge | Dissolve the Drudge, refund 1 500 mL to player |
| Drudge Electrode (ON mode) + attack swing | Send "fire now" signal to all owned Drudges within 16 blocks |
| Drudge Electrode (ON mode) + right-click SSC | Birth a new Drudge (degree gate + 3 000 mL cost) |

### Acquisition: Birthing via SSC + Electrode

1. Place an SSC with blood available.
2. Hold the Drudge Electrode in ON mode and right-click the SSC.
3. Degree gate: player must be at Degree 3 (Initiate) or higher (`drudgeRequiredDegree`, configurable).
4. Blood cost: 3 000 mL drained from player.
5. SSC cap: max 3 Drudges per SSC (configurable). Attempt beyond cap returns a flavour message.
6. Spawns a Drudge at the SSC position, bound to it, at half charge.

### SSC as Hub: `SemiSentientConstructBlockEntity`

The SSC now implements `IBloodReservoir` so it can hold its own blood volume (max 30 000 mL, refillable by Dendritic Distributors or other sources). Every 10 ticks it scans for nearby Drudges whose `homePos` matches its position and refills their `bloodCharge` by `REFILL_RATE` x 10 = 500 mL per scan (1,000 mL per second at 20 TPS).

Right-clicking the SSC with an empty hand now displays the status of all bound Drudges and the SSC's own blood level.

### Config Keys (`HemoServerConfig`, section `drudge`)

| Key | Default | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| `drudgeLeashRadius` | 24 | Max blocks from SSC before Drudge returns |
| `drudgeMaxPerSSC` | 3 | Max Drudges per SSC |
| `drudgeBirthCost` | 3000.0 | mL cost to birth a Drudge |
| `drudgeRogueTimeoutTicks` | 200 | Ticks stuck before going Rogue |
| `drudgeActionCostMultiplier` | 1.5 | Blood cost multiplier for Drudge actions |
| `drudgeCooldownMultiplier` | 2 | Cooldown multiplier for Drudge actions |
| `drudgeRequiredDegree` | 3 | Minimum degree to birth a Drudge |
| `drudgeWorkRadius` | 12 | Radius (blocks) for target scanning |
